title: Jahnavi Harrison
description: Jahnavi Harrison is a musician, writer, artist and practitioner of bhakti - yoga. She spent her formative years at Bhaktivedanta Manor in England, in a rich environment where mantra chanting and sacred art were a part of every day life. With a background in Western and Eastern classical music and dance, she has tried to pursue a path of self realisation and service through artistic expression. For nearly 20 years she has offered her voice and violin playing in the performance of original spiritual music and mantra kirtan, in diverse venues all over the world. She aspires to create art and facilitate experiences which heal, uplift and nourish the spirit. Now based in California; she regularly leads live gatherings, sound bath experiences, concerts and retreat s. Over the years Jahnavi has collaborated regularly with artists such as Deva Premal and Miten, Jai Uttal, Krishna Das, Snatam Kaur, Gaura Vani, and most recently, with Willow Smith with the EP Rise (2020). title: Tito Nieves - 50 Años La Historia Continua
description: Tito Nieves, born Humberto Nieves on June 4, 1958, in Río Piedras, Puerto Rico, is known as the "Pavarotti of Salsa" for his clear and powerful voice. Moving to New York City as a child, he grew up in a family of musicians & began his professional career in 1975 with Orquesta Cimarrón. He later worked with Héctor Lavoe, debuted with Johnny Ortiz's Taibori in 1978, and co-founded Conjunto Clásico, recording eight albums with the group before launching his solo career. His solo debut Classic (1988) went gold, followed by Yo Quiero Cantar (1989), which also went gold and featured the groundbreaking English-language salsa hit "I'll Always Love You." His 1990 album Déjame Vivir achieved platinum status, and I Like It Like That (1997), an all-English salsa album, brought mainstream exposure, including a performance with Stevie Wonder at the Alma Awards. Tito's later albums, including Dale Cara a la Vida (1998) and Clase Aparte (1999), showcase his blend of salsa, pop, and R&B influences.

description: FITZGERALDS NIGHTCLUB PRESENTS: Robert Ellis at FITZGERALDS Nightclub w/ special guest Philip Bowen $25 General Admission / Reserved Tables Available Recorded live to tape in just two days, Robert Ellis's exquisite new album, Yesterday's News, is as stripped-down as it gets, with the celebrated songwriter and producer's delicate, reedy tenor accompanied only by nylon string guitar, upright bass, and the occasional piece of handheld percussion. The arrangements are harmonically sophisticated here, drawing on the open tunings and intricate fingerpicking of English songwriters like Nick Drake or Richard Thompson, and Ellis's performances are similarly subtle and nuanced, tapping into the bittersweet longing of Chet Baker and the playful poignancy of Bill Evans and Jim Hall. While that might seem surprising coming off 2019's raucous Texas Piano Man, subverting expectations is nothing new for Ellis. Born and raised outside Houston, he gained early acclaim for his piercing introspection and absorbing narratives, but over the course of five solo albums, he flirted with everything from Paul Simon and John Prine to Elton John and Joni Mitchell in a series of sonic and visual transformations that ran the gamut from Redneck Steely Dan to Lone Star Liberace. NPR hailed his , "rdquo" -> musical daring and impeccable songcraft," while Rolling Stone praised his , "rdquo" -> sharp eye for storytelling," and the New York Times lauded his writing as an emotional , "rdquo" -> gut punch." Yesterday's News marks Ellis's debut LP for Niles City Records, an outgrowth of the famed Niles City Sound studio he and longtime collaborator Josh Block run in Fort Worth, TX. title: TERRAPIN FLYER: A Grateful Dead Tribute @ FITZGERALDS!
description: FITZGERALDS NIGHTCLUB PRESENTS: TERRAPIN FLYER: A Grateful Dead Tribute $25 General Admission // $30/seat Reserved Tables For more than 25 years, Terrapin Flyer has been a powerhouse of the national music scene, renowned for their faithful yet adventurous interpretations of Grateful Dead classics. Originally formed in 1999, the band has built a storied legacy through long-term collaborations with Dead legends like Melvin Seals, Vince Welnick, and Tom Constanten, earning them a spot in Rolling Stone's "Guide to the Grateful Dead." By blending tight musicianship with free-flowing improvisation and a deep reverence for jazz, blues, and bluegrass, the current lineup---featuring Josh Olken, Wavy Dave, Jon Reed, Michael Cole, and Doug Hagman---channels the authentic spirit of a true Dead show where every performance is a unique, soul-stirring experience. title: Good Night, Oscar
address: 987-D Lomas Santa Fe Drive, Solana Beach, CA, 92075
description: He was the funniest man in the room. And the most unfiltered. North Coast Repertory Theatre presents the West Coast Premiere of Good Night, Oscar, Pulitzer Prize winner Doug Wright's compassionate and wickedly funny portrait of Oscar Levant — pianist, actor, composer, and legendary wit whose sharp tongue was matched only by his profound musical genius. Set during a fateful 1958 appearance on The Jack Paar Show, this electrifying play captures one unforgettable night in the life of Hollywood's most neurotic and uncensored personality: a tortured artist wrestling with mental illness, addiction, and the price of fame, yet never losing his capacity for devastating honesty and breathtaking artistry. On Broadway, Sean Hayes won the 2023 Tony Award for Best Actor in a Play for his performance as Levant. Equal parts comedy and tragedy, Good Night, Oscar is a love letter to the golden age of television and a showcase for theatrical virtuosity — the story of a man performing himself for an audience, decades before the internet made everyone do it.

venue: Lakeside Community Center,9841 Vine St, Lakeside, CA 92040, USA
description: Hawktober is our annual celebration of local birds of prey, including hawks, owls, and falcons. This marks the event's eighth year offering FREE workshops at parks, campgrounds and wilderness preserves across San Diego County.  Events are free and open to all ages, starting October 3. Explore multiple workshops to meet different birds and rangers.  What to Expect:    * Live raptors: Meet ambassador birds like hawks, owls, and falcons up close and learn about their unique behaviors and adaptations.   * Fun facts: Discover how these birds live, what they eat, how they hunt, when they're active, and special traits like speed, camouflage, or night vision.   * Bird tales: Each event features different birds—each with a name and story—shared by passionate rangers.   * Special perk: Grab limited-edition Hawktober trading cards (while supplies last), complete with stats like wingspan, weight, and fun facts.  For more information, visit sdparks.org/hawktober https://www.sdparks.org/hawktober/ .

Día de los Muertos, or Day of the Dead, is a Mexican tradition that honors and remembers loved ones who have passed. At the heart of the celebration are remembrance, family, and community. As part of the museum’s celebration, guests will have the opportunity to experience traditional elements of Día de los Muertos while surrounded by some of the world’s most beautiful and historic vehicles.

title: Art Glass Guild Show and Sale
address: 1770 Village Pl, San Diego, CA, 92101
description: The Art Glass Guild will be hosting their 2026 Fall Patio Show and Sale on October 10th and 11th. This show is the largest Art Glass show in Southern California and is focused on showcasing art created by local San Diego Glass Artists. Visitors will see the patio full of juried artists exhibiting their creations as they stroll through Spanish Village Art Center in Balboa Park. Beautiful art glass exhibiting techniques such as: blown, fused, torch, stained, cast, and etched will be on display with the artist right there to explain or show how it is done. There will be entertainment for all including, a demonstration featuring torch-work, as well as an area for children and adults alike to create their own unique mosaic art piece to take home. The Art Glass Guild is a non-profit art education center, focused on supporting local glass artists as well as other San Diego non-profits with art related programs benefiting the community. “This is a fun family outing to see an array of beautiful art glass, glass demonstrations and free mosaic make and take and also to support our local artists,” says Helen Munroe, Fused Glass Artist and member of The Art Glass Guild. The event is free to the public and pet friendly.

title: Pumpkin Chunkin’
venue: San Diego Air and Space Museum
address: 2001 Pan American Plaza, San Diego, CA, 92101
description: Get ready for a day of engineering, coding, creativity, and flying pumpkins! Pumpkin Chunkin’ is returning to the San Diego Air & Space Museum on October 10, from 10 am to 1 pm bringing hands-on STEM challenges and plenty of Halloween fun for kids and families. This year, we’re excited to welcome a local high school robotics team, who will show visitors some of their amazing robot creations and demonstrate what goes into designing, building, and coding a competition robot. Young engineers can then try their own hand at solving Halloween-themed challenges throughout the museum. Activities will include: Build a Catapult: Design and construct a catapult, then see how far you can launch a candy pumpkin! Pumpkin Parachutes: Create a parachute designed to help a pumpkin make a safe landing. 3D Pen Spider Webs: Experiment with 3D pens to create creepy-crawly spider webs. Code a Mouse: Program a robotic mouse to navigate its way through a maze. Create a Monster: Use if-then statements to design a monster that reacts to different situations. And, of course, the highlight of Pumpkin Chunkin’ is the moment everyone waits for the PUMPKIN DROP! Watch as pumpkins take flight in a spectacular finale that combines a little Halloween fun with a lot of physics and engineering. There will be one small difference this year: the museum is currently covered in scaffolding as part of ongoing work on the building. So a new and exciting pumpkin platform will be used. Halloween Fun for Everyone Pumpkin Chunkin’ is included with museum admission, and October is Kids Free Month at the San Diego Air & Space Museum! During October, up to two children per one paid adult admission can visit the museum for free. Youth groups are welcome, too! Groups of 10–25 youth and their chaperones can attend for free with advance registration. To preregister your group, email education@sdasm.org . Costumes are welcome! Come dressed as your favorite astronaut, scientist, robot, monster, or anything else you can imagine. Join us for Pumpkin Chunkin’ and discover that some of the best Halloween fun comes with a little engineering mixed in!

Whether you are fishing or not, participate in the art of gyotaku and print your own fish with simple ink and paper. title: The CEO Within: For Fiction Authors Wanting To Make Money From Their Work
address: All over the world from, San Diego, CA
description: Most fiction authors think they’re struggling because they need more time, better marketing, more discipline, or a bigger audience. Usually, that’s not the real problem. The real problem is that every author who wants to make money from their books is actually trying to perform four very different jobs at the same time—and most authors are unknowingly neglecting at least one of them. In this highly interactive workshop, attendees will discover the four roles that exist inside every successful author business: The Storyteller, The Visionary, The Worker Bee, and The Manager. Through self-assessment, discussion, and real-world examples, authors will identify exactly where they’re strongest, where they’re struggling, and why they may feel stuck, overwhelmed, or frustrated despite working hard. Then comes the fun part. Participants will choose their own adventure, diving into the role that needs the most attention and leaving with practical action steps tailored to their specific situation. Attendees leave with greater clarity, renewed motivation, and a personalized roadmap for becoming the CEO of their author business instead of feeling buried by it.

description: Presented by the Del Mar Historical Society as part of its ongoing mission to preserve and celebrate the history and culture of our unique seaside community, and especially to honor the many people who have helped shape the culture and spirit of surfing over the years. At the heart of the festival is a multi-generational Surfers Reunion, bringing together people who rode Del Mar's waves in the 1950s and 60s—and even earlier— alongside today's surfers and the next generations to follow. By bringing together stories, art, film science and shared memories, Surf Del Mar Festival honors the pioneers who helped shape surf culture while inspiring future generations to care for the coast, the ocean, and the traditions that grew from them.

title: The Unsaid: Writing Through Silence, Secrecy & Omission
address: All over the world from, San Diego, CA
description: Some stories and poems are shaped as much by what remains unsaid as by what is spoken. In this two-part generative workshop for poets, fiction writers, memoirists, and hybrid writers, explore how silence, omission, secrecy, emotional restraint, and gaps in knowledge can create tension, complexity, and resonance on the page. Through readings, discussion, prompts, and in-class writing, participants will examine how writers use absence as a craft tool and how family secrets, cultural silences, missing histories, and unanswered questions can become powerful literary material. Read and discuss work by writers such as Yusef Komunyakaa, Natasha Trethewey, Agha Shahid Ali, Lucille Clifton, Eduardo C. Corral, Jhumpa Lahiri, Alexander Chee, James Baldwin, Akwaeke Emezi, and Jesmyn Ward. The first session will focus on silence as craft, emotional restraint, and writing around what cannot be directly said. The second session will explore revision strategies, omission as a source of tension and meaning, and will conclude with a supportive sharing session for both poetry and prose writers.

title: Wings Over Water
address: 1875 El Prado, San Diego, CA, 92101
description: Across the heartland of North America, a wetland kingdom of connected rivers, lakes, and waterways has provided an oasis for wildlife since the retreat of the last ice age over 10,000 years ago. Today, these water highways are home to countless species. Alongside herds of bison in the Great Plains and salamanders in the smallest ponds, millions of frequent fliers rely on this pristine wilderness for survival.Wings Over Water, narrated by Michael Keaton, follows three magnificent bird species—the Sandhill Crane, the Yellow Warbler, and the Mallard Duck—as they migrate along these epic “flyways.” With extraordinary footage brought to life on the Heikoff Giant Dome IMAX® screen, audiences can fly alongside these incredible birds and experience the wonder of one of North America’s most diverse and untouched ecosystems.

description: He was the funniest man in the room. And the most unfiltered. North Coast Repertory Theatre presents the West Coast Premiere of Good Night, Oscar, Pulitzer Prize winner Doug Wright's compassionate and wickedly funny portrait of Oscar Levant — pianist, actor, composer, and legendary wit whose sharp tongue was matched only by his profound musical genius. Set during a fateful 1958 appearance on The Jack Paar Show, this electrifying play captures one unforgettable night in the life of Hollywood's most neurotic and uncensored personality: a tortured artist wrestling with mental illness, addiction, and the price of fame, yet never losing his capacity for devastating honesty and breathtaking artistry. On Broadway, Sean Hayes won the 2023 Tony Award for Best Actor in a Play for his performance as Levant. Equal parts comedy and tragedy, Good Night, Oscar is a love letter to the golden age of television and a showcase for theatrical virtuosity — the story of a man performing himself for an audience, decades before the internet made everyone do it.

description: Taking turns at an onstage piano, the dual tribute artists of the Billy Joel/Elton John Face 2 Face? Tribute Show conjure the beloved songsters in both sound and image. Backed by his band The Stranger, Levittown, NY native Mike Santoro?s fingers flash up and down the keys before he jumps up to grab the mic to belt out such high-energy Billy Joel classics as ?Uptown Girl? and ?Only the Good Die Young.? For the second half of the roughly three-hour show, Ronnie Smith dons the iconic sunglasses and bedazzled suits of Elton John as he charts his style from the ?70s to the present. Bittersweet anthems such as ?Rocket Man (I Think It?s Going to Be a Long, Long Time)? mix with more whimsical material such as ?Crocodile Rock? and the fictional rock-group narrative ?Bennie and the Jets.? During each engaging, interactive show, both acts aim to channel the spirit of their originals so well that audiences will forget they?re a tribute!

description: Longevity in music comes through pushing yourself and expanding the possibilities of your sound. This has never been more true for Copeland. The band, which originally formed in Lakeland, Florida in 2001, has unveiled six albums, spanning from their 2003s debut Beneath Medicine Tree to 2016s Ixora. While they began as a rock band, Copelands music has explored multiple genres and pulled in various stylistic influences like electronic and symphonic. In the past the musicians have aptly melded these styles, creating a unique amalgam of sounds. This time they wanted to take each sound and style and push it to its logical extreme.

title: Armand Hammer with Quelle Chris and Open Mike Eagle
description: For nearly a decade as a duo, and longer still as solo artists, Armand Hammer have left a palpable mark on modern rap and hip-hop. At turns both sharp-witted and soul-crushing, their lyrics unspool threads of socio-political, historical, and philosophical import with a potent blend of incisive critique, gallows humor, and narrative élan. Mercy is the first Armand Hammer album since 2023's We Buy Diabetic Test Strips, a project that The Observer (UK) described as "an exceptional record that deserves your time and headphones" and The Line Of Best Fit deemed "their headiest and most impressive work thus far." On 2021's Haram, their first with The Alchemist, the duo "drag postcolonial wounds onto the examination table" (Pitchfork). Beats Per Minute called it "a tremendous success." Earlier this year, billy woods released GOLLIWOG, ", "rdquo" -> a densely poetic, totally masterful tour de force" (Rolling Stone) and "one of 2025's truly essential albums" (The FADER). Meanwhile, ELUCID's "enthralling" (MOJO) 2024 album REVELATOR was described by Pitchfork as "soul food for those who know a better world is possible if we're willing to fight for it." The New York Times, in naming REVELATOR one of their Best Albums Of 2024, called it "a dense, overdriven, fiercely abrasive album that cranks up the tradition of Public Enemy's Bomb Squad productions for 21st-century impact."

venue: Oakoasis County Preserve,12620 Wildcat Canyon Rd, Lakeside, CA 92040, USA
description: Visit real astronomers from the San Diego Astronomy Association and look through their big, beautiful telescopes at Mother Nature's night light display.  The evening starts off with a short, ranger-led, twilight hike down our HAUNTED TRAIL at 6 p.m., just for October!  It may be too cold to see bats and scorpions, but it should be a great night for stargazing! The evening continues with stars and refreshments. description: Sensory-Friendly Quiet Mornings at the Museum The Museum’s sensory-friendly quiet hours are held every Sunday from 10 a.m. to 11 a.m. This time is dedicated to creating a calmer, quieter museum experience. We remain open to the public during this time, and all are welcome to visit the Museum. During this time, specific exhibit features in the main Museum building will be turned off to minimize audio and visual stimulation. Noise-blocking headphones are free for check-out at the main Admissions desk and the entrance to the Cannibals: Myth & Reality exhibition, Exhibit features in the Cannibals: Myth & Reality exhibit will remain on, and all exhibits will be fully turned on at 11 a.m. Admission purchased during sensory-friendly quiet hours is the same as standard admission and applies to the entire day. title: Art Glass Guild Show and Sale
address: 1770 Village Pl, San Diego, CA, 92101
description: The Art Glass Guild will be hosting their 2026 Fall Patio Show and Sale on October 10th and 11th. This show is the largest Art Glass show in Southern California and is focused on showcasing art created by local San Diego Glass Artists. Visitors will see the patio full of juried artists exhibiting their creations as they stroll through Spanish Village Art Center in Balboa Park. Beautiful art glass exhibiting techniques such as: blown, fused, torch, stained, cast, and etched will be on display with the artist right there to explain or show how it is done. There will be entertainment for all including, a demonstration featuring torch-work, as well as an area for children and adults alike to create their own unique mosaic art piece to take home. The Art Glass Guild is a non-profit art education center, focused on supporting local glass artists as well as other San Diego non-profits with art related programs benefiting the community. “This is a fun family outing to see an array of beautiful art glass, glass demonstrations and free mosaic make and take and also to support our local artists,” says Helen Munroe, Fused Glass Artist and member of The Art Glass Guild. The event is free to the public and pet friendly.

title: Interpol - North America Tour 2026 with DIIV
description: This Mirror Weighs a Ton, finds the band turning inward while continuing to move forward. Across the record, reflection, distortion and perception become a lens through which familiar shapes are refracted into something slightly alien, as if seen through a different kind of light. Synthesizers, strings, acoustic guitars and percussion are integrated into the fabric of the songs, expanding the palette while revealing colors already latent within it. Nothing feels imposed. Instead, the additions deepen the band?s language of restraint, atmosphere and tension. The result is an album that feels expansive, uncanny and alive with forward motion, not a reinvention but an evolution that allows Interpol to continue transforming without losing their identity.

description: Hawktober is our annual celebration of local birds of prey, including hawks, owls, and falcons. Explore multiple workshops to meet different birds and rangers.  What to Expect:    * Live raptors: Meet ambassador birds like hawks, owls, and falcons up close and learn about their unique behaviors and adaptations.   * Fun facts: Discover how these birds live, what they eat, how they hunt, when they're active, and special traits like speed, camouflage, or night vision.   * Bird tales: Each event features different birds—each with a name and story—shared by passionate rangers.   * Special perk: Grab limited-edition Hawktober trading cards (while supplies last), complete with stats like wingspan, weight, and fun facts. BIO: A little drama never hurt anybody... Emei knows how to bring it too. She's an unabashed , "rdquo" -> theater kid" who grew up into an Ivy League-educated pop femme fatale at the helm of a crazy, candy-coated, and colorful world of her own making. With a bold voice that's as vibrant as her personality, the New Jersey-born Chinese-American songstress delivers clever and catchy anthems meant to be blasted out loud. After gathering over a quarter-of-a-billion streams, selling out shows, and attracting multi-GRAMMY® Award-winning mega-producer Ricky Reed [Lizzo, Leon Bridges, Camila Cabello, Phantogram, Jon Batiste] to her corner, she embraces her theatricality on her Night At The Opera EP [Atlantic Records / Nice Life]. , "rdquo" -> I grew up doing theater, but the vibe changed when my pop music career started," she states. , "rdquo" -> I wanted to lean into being a theater kid again. This project is definitely a homecoming. My subconscious bullied teenage brain is always like, 'You don't want to try so hard. Just be cool'. But fuck that! I like trying hard. It's part of who I am. I care about every little detail. So, you're going to get all of the pain, emotion, and drama from me!"

title: An Evening With Steve Dawson with special guests Jason Adasiewicz, Jason Roebke, Diane Christiansen and Alton Smith
description: One of the lynchpins of Chicagos flourishing songwriter scene is Steve Dawson, a songwriter and vocalist who elevates everything he touches. - WBEZ Chicago An evocative, brilliant songwriter who imbues his songs and recordings with folk, country, and a smattering of soul he should, by all rights, be a household name. - Popmatters Steve Dawson will look back over 35 years of songs and music making, including songs from his first Chicago band, Stump The Host, through Dolly Varden, Funeral Bonsai Wedding and up to his more recent critically acclaimed solo albums, Ghosts, and At The Bottom of a Canyon in the Branches of a Tree. Over the course of 6 albums with Dolly Varden, 4 solo albums, and 2 albums with the jazz / folk combo, Funeral Bonsai Wedding, Dawson has delved into all corners of American music and dug deep into the mysteries and wonders of life, mortality, love and memory. Dawson will be joined by a few guest musicians for this evenings show. Originally from San Diego, California, he spent his teen years in Hailey, Idaho, where he learned guitar and started writing songs. After a few years at the Berklee School of Music in Boston, Dawson moved to Chicago and formed the band, Stump the Host, with his future wife, artist and singer, Diane Christiansen. Later he formed, recorded and toured with Dolly Varden and Funeral Bonsai Wedding. More recently he has created critically acclaimed solo albums for the Pravda record label. Dawson also teaches songwriting at the legendary Old Town School of Folk Music and co-wrote a book on songwriting and the creative process with Mark Caro called, Take It To The Bridge: Unlocking The Great Songs Inside You. In 2020 Dawson was awarded the Esteemed Artist Award from the City of Chicago.

title: BEAT: Belew/Vai/Levin/Bozzio Performing the Music of KING CRIMSON
description: Following more than 100 acclaimed performances across North and South America, Europe, and Japan, BEAT returns this fall for the last North American tour. Former King Crimson members Adrian Belew and Tony Levin are joined by guitar virtuoso Steve Vai and legendary drummer Terry Bozzio to perform the music of the three landmark 1980s King Crimson albums---Discipline, Beat, and Three of a Perfect Pair. Rather than attempting to recreate the original recordings, BEAT brings this extraordinary music to life with the spirit, precision, and adventurousness that made it so enduring. Whether you've lived with these albums for decades or are discovering them for the first time, this is the final opportunity to experience one of progressive music's most celebrated catalogs performed by four of the best musicians on the planet.

venue: The San Diego LGBT Community Center
source: The San Diego LGBT Community Center
description: It's time for self-care with our free, confidential HIV/HCV testing and STI screenings in a compassionate and sex-positive environment with connections to health care and resources. Make your appointment today - call us at 619.487.9980 or email bethegeneration@thecentersd.org to make an appointment. We are open Monday-Friday 10am-7pm and Saturdays 10am-3pm by appointment. Walk-ins will be accepted based on availability. Please note that we do not offer MPOX testing as part of our testing services, please call 211 for testing assistance. Es hora de cuidarte con nuestras pruebas gratuitas y confidenciales de VIH/VHC y exámenes de detección de ITS en un entorno compasivo y sexualmente positivo con conexiones con recursos y atención médica. Haz tu cita hoy: llámanos al 619.487.9980 o envía un correo electrónico a bethegeneration@thecentersd.org para programar una cita. Abrimos de lunes a viernes de 10am a 7pm y sabados de 10am a 3pm con cita previa. Se aceptarán visitas sin cita previa según disponibilidad. Ten en cuenta que no ofrecemos pruebas MPOX como parte de nuestros servicios de pruebas; llame al 211 para obtener ayuda con las pruebas.

venue: The San Diego LGBT Community Center
source: The San Diego LGBT Community Center
description: Acompáñanos a celebrar el Día de las Rebeldías Lésbicas con Cruzando la Línea: Cultura y Rebeldía Lésbica en la Frontera, un panel de discusión presentado por Latin@x Services at The Center. Cuatro lideresas se reunirán para conversar sobre lo que significa crear, resistir y nombrarnos desde la frontera, y compartir sus perspectivas sobre cultura, arte y activismo lésbico en la región fronteriza. title: The Burney Sisters
description: The Burney Sisters are a powerhouse sibling duo redefining indie-folk with their soulful harmonies, heartfelt lyrics, and magnetic stage presence. Originally from the Midwest, sisters Emma and Bella Burney create music that blends folk, indie, and Americana into a sound that feels both timeless and fresh. Drawing inspiration from iconic artists like Paul Simon and Lake Street Dive, as well as contemporary trailblazers like Lizzy McAlpine, Madison Cunningham, Phoebe Bridgers, and First Aid Kit The Burney Sisters bridge generations with a style that is uniquely their own. Emma's multi-instrumental talents---on piano, violin, guitar, and cello---pair seamlessly with Bella's commanding basslines, showcasing a maturity and versatility far beyond their years. Their music explores themes of love, resilience, and self-discovery with a raw honesty that resonates deeply with fans of all ages. For the past eight years, The Burney Sisters have traveled extensively, performing across the U.S., Canada, and the Caribbean. Their journey has not only shaped their sound but also fueled their passion for connecting through music.

Return the toolkit & all contents to the same location on 10/13 or 10/20. </p><p>Questions? title: Women’s Book Club (In Person)
venue: The San Diego LGBT Community Center
source: The San Diego LGBT Community Center
description: This peer-led Book Club welcomes lesbian, bisexual, queer, transgender, and questioning women of all ages to join readers in a friendly, thought-provoking discussion related to the month’s book selection. All book selections emphasize works written by and about women and vary in genre, ranging from non-fiction to poetry to historical literature to romance to science fiction to graphic novels. When: 2nd Wednesday, 5-6:30 pm Where: The Center Library, 3909 Centre St. San Diego, CA 92103 Contact: For more information on the group, please contact women@thecentersd.org. Phone: ‪(619) 692-2077 x134 October: The Valley of the Dolls by Jacqueline Susann Published in 1966, it was the biggest selling book of the year. It has since gone on to become one of the best selling novels of all time. The story follows Ann and Neely, young women who move to New York in 1945 to seek fame and fortune. They love, they social climb, and meet all sorts of people that help and hurt them along the way. This book has everything! The rich, the famous, the drugs, the high life and the low. The book was controversial at the time because it was thought that certain characters were based on such folk as Judy Garland and Dean Martin and, famously, Ethel Merman. The book was also made into the great campy movie with Patty Duke and her dolls. Get ready to read a true phenomenon. November: Positive Obsession by Susana M. Morris This is a biography of Octavia Butler, one of the true trailblazers of Science Fiction writing. The book shows how Butler was truly influenced by and was a mirror to the world around her, as well as quite the future teller. From the Civil Rights Movement to Reaganomics to queer and gender studies, Butler's tales of facism, gender violence, climate chaos and relationships have influenced writers of every genre. Truly ahead of her time and timeless.

title: White Denim w. Arc Iris
description: Ive always wanted to make work thats a reflection of my life experience, says singer-guitarist James Petralli, leader of venturous L.A.-based rockers White Denim. The just-below-the-surface significance to 13 as an album title is that I was born on the thirteenth of August. 13 in numerology can signify independence, creativity, and a solid foundation, but inversely is often considered to be unlucky and can signify chaos and misfortune. Like everyone, I can certainly see both sides in my life.13 also happens to be the thirteenth album of White Denims career. An incandescent, groove-heavy alchemy of rock, funk, dub, soul and down-dirty blues and plenty more besides its imbued with the same questing spirit thats been the bands trademark since first starting in Austin, Texas, some 20 years ago.Petrallis wide-ranging musical appetites have become more voracious over time. The sounds and textures of 13 are informed by everyone from Scritti Politti to The Gap Band, Terry Reid to King Tubby, Caetano Veloso to John Cale, Stevie Wonder to 80s-era Steve Winwood. Such diversity is reflected in multi-faceted gems like (God Created) Lock And Key, Only A Fool and Thats Rap.The seed of the project is rooted in the irresistible Chew Nails. Its a straightforward glam-rock tune, says Petralli. My take on the New York Groove, which is itself a take on the Bo Diddley beat. It has a big ol guitar riff and a singalong chorus. Its familiar territory for me, yet the vocal is perhaps more forward than most things Ive done for the band. Its the song that made me feel like I was definitely making a White Denim album.The duality of 13 is immediately apparent. The pungent funk-blues of opener (God Created) Lock And Key begins with a piece of waggish self-mythology On the thirteenth day God created White Denim but soon goes somewhere darker. This is a Beefheart / Sun Ra sort of thing, Petralli explains. I hope that its a somewhat terrifying, startling, and visceral piece for everyone that hears it. Everything I say in that song is the truth. Its about power, generational cycles of abuse, shame, violence, and survival. The things that we all understand and know and see and push down to get through the day.

title: Vape! The Grease Parody
description: Vape! The Grease Parody is a hilariously unhinged spoof of the iconic and timeless musical film Grease. The show pokes loving fun at all of the wonderful moments, sexual innuendos, outrageous characters, rivalries and secret romances from the original. The hair products may have changed, but the drama, the rivalries, and the thirst for hallway clout remain timeless. It is the musical you know and love, but dragged through a cloud of strawberry scented vapor and a TikTok filter. It's the show that you want (Ooh! Ooh! Ooh, honey!) Don't miss the Chicago premiere of this hit musical, straight from NYC. GREASE is no longer the word. Now the word is VAPE! - New York Post A must-see! A fun, irreverent night out. I couldn't stop laughing. - Hollywood Press Corps VAPE! is the one that you want! Clever, goofy and camp. - Theater Pizzazz Brash, fast and unapologetically smart. - Theaterscene.net VAPE! The Grease Parody is 85 minutes with no intermission.

This is an American Indian revenge story written by one of the new masters of horror, Stephen Graham Jones.<br><br></p>

title: Sober Curious

source: The San Diego LGBT Community Center
description: Sober Curious is a welcoming space for LGBTQ+ community members exploring their relationship with alcohol and other substances. Whether you're cutting back, taking a break, staying sober, or just curious, come connect, heal, and have fun in a safe, affirming environment. No labels, no pressure. Just curiosity, support, and community. Your goals. Your pace. Your journey. When: Thursdays, 5:00 – 6:00 PM Where: The Center, 3909 Centre St, San Diego Contact: counseling@thecentersd.org

title: Jazz in the SIDEBAR w/ THE ANDY BROWN TRIO!
description: FITZGERALDS SIDEBAR PRESENTS: THE ANDY BROWN TRIO! (w/ Greg Fishman on tenor saxophone and Jake Vinsel on bass) Andy Brown is a musician based in Chicago who specializes in what he calls , "rdquo" -> old-school jazz guitar." Howard Reich in the Chicago Tribune called him "One of Chicago's most appealing jazz guitarists...uncounted Chicago jazz artists have collaborated with Brown on club dates and recording sessions, and they know better than anyone the depth of his work and unpretentiousness of his manner...for all his easy going virtuosity, he places the emphasis on musical phrase rather than pyrotechnics." Andy has made many festival appearances around the world including performances in Brazil, Europe and Canada. His latest CD is the critically acclaimed 2023 album Good Atmosphere. In this trio setting he'll be joined by two Chicago jazz veterans on bass and drums. FREE SHOW! Click , "rdquo" -> Book Now" to RSVP for guaranteed entry Grab dinner before the show at BABYGOLD BARBECUE ***PARKING*** There is rather limited street parking in the area, we recommend arriving by rideshare, bicycle, or rickshaw.

title: Vape! The Grease Parody
description: Vape! The Grease Parody is a hilariously unhinged spoof of the iconic and timeless musical film Grease. The show pokes loving fun at all of the wonderful moments, sexual innuendos, outrageous characters, rivalries and secret romances from the original. The hair products may have changed, but the drama, the rivalries, and the thirst for hallway clout remain timeless. It is the musical you know and love, but dragged through a cloud of strawberry scented vapor and a TikTok filter. It's the show that you want (Ooh! Ooh! Ooh, honey!) Don't miss the Chicago premiere of this hit musical, straight from NYC. GREASE is no longer the word. Now the word is VAPE! - New York Post A must-see! A fun, irreverent night out. I couldn't stop laughing. - Hollywood Press Corps VAPE! is the one that you want! Clever, goofy and camp. - Theater Pizzazz Brash, fast and unapologetically smart. - Theaterscene.net VAPE! The Grease Parody is 85 minutes with no intermission.

description: Join co-editors Océane Boulais and Theodora Mautz for a conversation about the community-led zine in situ, born at Scripps Institution of Oceanography. Discover how graduate students, postdocs, and staff transform scientific experiences—from coral reef surveys and whale encounters to ice cores and lab life—into visual art, photography, poetry, and multimedia storytelling for the zine. Proceeds from the zine and community support go toward printing costs, art supplies, and events that keep collective creative action alive at Scripps, making in situ as much a grassroots organizing effort as a publication. Océane and Theodora will share the evolution of in situ , from its inaugural Seas of Change issue to its current Countercurrents volume, and explore how creative expression can complement scientific inquiry, build community across disciplines, and offer new ways of understanding our oceans. Stay for the end of the presentation, where a surprise instrument invites you to play the ocean’s frequencies yourself! The talk will take place at Mingei International Museum. Theodora Mautz is a PhD candidate in the Marine Biology program at Scripps Institution of Oceanography. She currently researches cephalopod reproduction. Océane Boulais is a PhD candidate in the Applied Ocean Science program at Scripps Institution of Oceanography. As an ecoacoustician, Océane listens to the ocean as a language of texture, color, and rhythm and then employs instruments to broadcast sound from healthy coral reefs into restoration reef sites, drawing coral and fish larvae home by sound via “acoustic enrichment”.

address: 1875 El Prado, San Diego, CA, 92101
description: Volcanoes have helped create our world. The continents, the air we breathe and even life itself have their origins in fire. These processes have created extraordinary ecosystems and wildlife habitats. The story of volcanoes is the story of the planet’s creation and the story of us. Volcanoes: The Fires of Creation , lets you witness the 2018 Kilauea eruption in Hawaii; see the archaeological remains of Pompeii, devastated almost 2,000 years ago by Mount Vesuvius; visit Mount Fuji in Japan, made up of three volcanoes—Fuji on top and two others hidden beneath; and marvel at the black molten lava of Ol Doinyo Lengai in Tanzania.

description: Celebrate Hispanic Heritage Month and Día de los Muertos with a festive evening of art, drinks, and local history! Join the San Diego History Center at Mujeres Brew House, San Diego’s first Latina-owned brewery, for a fun Paint & Sip experience. Enjoy a guided painting session led by local artist Maira Meza (@artehastalamuerte6), sip on your favorite drinks, and learn fascinating bits of local history from SDHC staff along the way. This month, we’re celebrating Día de los Muertos by painting alebrijes—colorful, creatures rooted in Mexican folk art. As you create your own alebrije, learn about their cultural significance and how they have become associated with Día de los Muertos celebrations. No painting experience needed! Whether you’re an experienced artist or picking up a paintbrush for the first time, this evening is all about having fun and getting creative. All painting materials provided Tickets: $30 — San Diego History Center Members $40 — General Admission

title: The Heavy Rotation Session 19 - Currents by Tame Impala
description: The Heavy Rotation is proud to be back at Three Top Lounge for their next session this time covering and listening to Currents by Tame Impala. If you are just hearing about The Heavy Rotation this is an idea between friends, Kalium Ewing and Grant Frahm, who were constantly sharing albums over text and wanted to connect through music in a more intentional way. They missed the feeling of hearing music in the same room and talking about it face to face. The club became their way of carving out time to slow down, listen together, and explore how music can hit differently within a community of strangers who become friends. This will be The Heavy Rotations 19th Session where they will be diving into the production and lyrics surrounding this specific album. Whether you've played this album hundreds of times, haven't listened to it in years, or will be hearing it front to back for the first time, all perspectives are welcome. Come ready to listen, question, challenge, and have an open and interesting conversation.

title: Laura Veirs w. Karl Blau
description: Laura Veirs returns with Temple Songs, her first album in four yearsand the first she has written, recorded, arranged, produced, and performed entirely on her own. I didnt know if I would write songs again, says Veirs, who spent the intervening years building a backyard studio, getting married, blending a family with four teenagers, deepening her visual art practice (painting), and expanding her music teaching. Turns out that period was a gathering phase. When I made the commitment to recording the album myself, the muse caught me again and it came together very quickly.Written and recorded in three months in the fall of 2025 in Veirs backyard Temple of Bloom studio, Temple Songs marks a new level of artistic independence. While 2022s Found Light (co-produced by Veirs and Shahzad Ismaily) was a declaration of autonomy, Temple Songs goes further: every creative decisionwhat to record, how to record it, and how it should soundwas Veirs alone. Made with just two mics and a laptop in a 10 x 14 room, the album feels unmistakably Veirs-ian, yet strikingly new.Veirs embraced the Japanese concept of wabi-sabi throughout the process, choosing not to pitch-correct vocals or edit out rough edges. I wanted to make something that sounds as organic and human as possible, she says. Mixing by Philip Weinrobe (Adrienne Lenker) adds sympathetic finishing touches to Veirs 14th solo album.Because the Temple of Bloom wasnt built for recording, the studio itself became a collaborator. Veirs paused takes for rain on the skylightor let it stay. She waited out neighbors conversations, raced to finish a sensitive vocal before a stump grinder roared to life, and included the presence of resident bluejays, passing crows, and other neighborhood sounds. These ambient intrusions lend the album an intimate, lived-in authenticity.Influences range from Mac DeMarcos commitment to trusting his personal taste to the anarchists and feminists of the late 1800s and their rallying cry, no gods, no masters. It was hard to get the white man off my shoulder, Veirs says. I wrestled with a lot of doubt. But there were many happy accidents and eventually I found a flowseeing the studio again, for the first time since my 20s, as a private place for exploration.Clocking in at a concise 30 minutes, Temple Songs 11 tracks capture a songwriter in peak form. The album is intimate, dreamy, brave and quietly defiant, built around Veirs intricate fingerstyle nylon-string guitar, vulnerable vocals, and bold electric guitar embellishments. Arc Still Bends reflects feelings of contemporary futility, offset by a hopeful chorus. Rivers Song, an ode to one of Veirs children, showcases her gift for simplicity and emotional precision. Pulse veers into art-experimental territory, culminating in a cacophonous duet between electric guitar and sax. No Masters is a sparse, punk rock call for collective self-determination, while Sunlight and Doom incorporates elemental fragments from the ancient Greek lyricist Sappho.

title: Osees ft. Brigid Dawson with Traps PS
description: Photo by Saskia Ludden The 12 tracks on ABOMINATION REVEALED AT LAST. are a pummeling, maniacal, and propulsive attack on the senses--a fitting reaction to a world suffering from genocide, environmental collapse, state sanctioned violence, progressing technocracy, and more. , "rdquo" -> Well this album just channelled out of the mist of atrocities swirling around the planet right now," songwriter John Dwyer explains. , "rdquo" -> AI empathy, genocides, social media data collection & addiction, the alignment of tech billionaires with the fascist overlords and their armada of dogs, civilians being kidnapped by bootlicking thugs, the death of due process...the list goes on and on. It's been a long year already." ABOMINATION REVEALED AT LAST and its singles have received acclaim from Stereogum, Aquarium Drunkard (review), FLOOD Magazine (review, premiere), Brooklyn Vegan, The Line of Best Fit, Northern Transmissions, RIFF Magazine, and many more. The LP was recorded by Enrique Tena Padilla, Mario Ramirez & Dwyer, mixed by Padilla and Dwyer, and mastered by JJ Golden. OSEES are John Dwyer (vocals/guitar/synths), Tom Dolas (guitar/samples/keys), Tim Hellman (bass), and Dan Rincon (drums)

title: Vape! The Grease Parody
description: Vape! The Grease Parody is a hilariously unhinged spoof of the iconic and timeless musical film Grease. The show pokes loving fun at all of the wonderful moments, sexual innuendos, outrageous characters, rivalries and secret romances from the original. The hair products may have changed, but the drama, the rivalries, and the thirst for hallway clout remain timeless. It is the musical you know and love, but dragged through a cloud of strawberry scented vapor and a TikTok filter. It's the show that you want (Ooh! Ooh! Ooh, honey!) Don't miss the Chicago premiere of this hit musical, straight from NYC. GREASE is no longer the word. Now the word is VAPE! - New York Post A must-see! A fun, irreverent night out. I couldn't stop laughing. - Hollywood Press Corps VAPE! is the one that you want! Clever, goofy and camp. - Theater Pizzazz Brash, fast and unapologetically smart. - Theaterscene.net VAPE! The Grease Parody is 85 minutes with no intermission.

title: Blake Whiten - Something To Say Tour
description: Wielding a broken-glass vocal on self-penned songs that cut straight to the bone, Enchntmnt / Warner Records singer-songwriter Blake Whiten is a 21-year-old instinctive songsmith raised in Six Mile, South Carolina, whose talent launched him from bedroom videos to the biggest stages in the world. Revealed as a generational diamond in the rough, raw emotion and heavy-hearted lyrics have earned Whiten over 150 million global streams in two years since his first public performance, with more to come. Growing up on everything from Keith Whitley to Nickelback, Whiten learned guitar at seven and was penning angsty tunes by 15. After discovering the depths of his raspy vocal, a cover of Morgan Wallens Im the Problem racked up 9 million views and sent him down a new path. His solo-written 2024 single Rollin Stone amassed over 120 million streams and his co-write on Bailey Zimmermans Holding On broke the Top 40 on Billboards Hot Country Songs chart. The self-penned 2025 EP debut Six Mile captured his essence, while SiriusXM, Spotify, Apple Music, Pandora, Country Now, Holler and All Country News have lined up in support. After headlining his Rollin Stone Tour and making his Grand Ole Opry debut in early 2026, Whitens first album Something to Say, features 12 co-written songs, as his confessional instincts collide with pitch-black alt-rock intensity. Currently on Bailey Zimmermans Different Night Same Rodeo Tour, hell take the stage in stadiums this summer for Wallens Still the Problem Tour 2026.Story Behind The Song Acoustic Experience includes:One Event TicketExclusive Access to the Fan Voted Story Behind The Song Acoustic ExperienceOne VIP-Exclusive Poster Signed by Blake WhitenOne Commemorative VIP LaminateEarly Entry (Where Applicable)Early Access Merchandise Shopping (Where Applicable)This package does NOT include a meet & greet with Blake Whiten.

title: JESSE ROPER Returns to FITZGERALDS Nightclub!
description: FITZGERALDS NIGHTCLUB PRESENTS: Jesse Roper Returns to FITZGERALDS Nightclub $20 General Admission / Reserved Tables Available Jesse Roper is a modern-day troubadour; a Canadian artist defined by his authenticity and adventurous spirit; guitar in hand and a grin on his face. Jesse, along with long-time bandmates the Pretty Good Band, has spent much of the last few years travelling the highways, byways and backroads of North America, bringing his own brand of modern, indie-infused Americana blues to fervent audiences across the continent. Known for his powerhouse live performances, Jesse is truly electrifying on stage - his soulful vocals expanding across silky guitars and hard-hitting grooves. You'd never guess that this soldier of the six string - all mischief, mayhem and virtuoso guitar playing - experienced crippling stage-fright long into his 20s. Today, the stage is his home and he's inviting you in, cold one in hand, for one helluva good time. Of course, he's more than a magnetising stage presence and great hair - Jesse has the goods to back this up. A master at connecting his personal experiences to his songwriting, he crafts wildly entertaining narratives of the challenges and eccentricities of life, pulling inspiration from all that surrounds him. His musings on love (both won and lost), the call of the road and the promise of what's round the corner draw similarities to JJ Cale, Leon Bridges, and Alabama Shakes. His innate musical talent and flexibility of style have seen him play with soul icon Booker T. Jones, rock veteran Colin James, blues belter Beth Hart, and Canadian legend Burton Cummings. Across streaming platforms, he's racked up over 500,000 monthly listeners and millions of streams. While based in Victoria BC, Jesse is back on the road with the Pretty Good Band throughout 2026. All seasoned musicians themselves, the band is Matt Reid (bass), Chris Van Sickle (keys), East Coast Pete (guitar) and Brent Norman (drums). , "rdquo" -> Each one of these guys on their own is funnier and smarter than I am, but somehow I'm the band leader," Jesse laughs. , "rdquo" -> I'm a lucky lead guy to have these cats in my band. They're Pretty Good." title: Meteorites as Artistic Matter
address: 1450 El Prado, San Diego, CA, 92101
description: Speakers: Ulrike Arnold , Artist; Gerard van Belle, PhD , Former Director of Science at Lowell Observatory; and Rachel Jans, PhD , Curator of Modern and Contemporary Art at The San Diego Museum of Art MOPA@SDMA Joan and Irwin Jacobs Theater Meteorites as Artistic Matter brings together internationally acclaimed artist Ulrike Arnold, astronomer Gerard van Belle, and the Museum’s Curator of Modern and Contemporary Art Rachel Jans, PhD, for a fascinating interdisciplinary conversation exploring the intersection of art, science, and the cosmos. Known for incorporating meteorite dust and pigments gathered from some of the world’s most remote landscapes into her paintings, Arnold will discuss how celestial and earthly materials become powerful artistic media. Joined by van Belle’s astronomical perspective and Jans’s expertise on the work of Sigmar Polke, a German artist also known for incorporating unconventional materials into his work, and contemporary artistic practice, this engaging guest lecture offers a rare opportunity to discover how meteorites inspire creativity, expand our understanding of materiality, and connect artistic expression with the vast universe beyond our planet. Following the lecture, guests are invited to enjoy a guided tour led by our docent team. Please note, this lecture is in-person only and held at the MOPA@SDMA Joan and Irwin Jacobs Theater in Balboa Park. $15 members and students | $20 seniors and military | $30 nonmembers This lecture is presented as a part of the Guest Lecture Series , which offers a platform for renowned scholars and experts from the art world to share their insights and knowledge on topics related to art history, art theory, and the museum’s collections.

title: Nat at Night
venue: San Diego Natural History Museum (The Nat)
address: 1788 El Prado, Balboa Park, San Diego, CA, 92101
description: On select Fridays, the San Diego Natural History Museum is open late just for you. Enjoy access to all open exhibitions and our rooftop deck for good views and great vibes. The rooftop is open to all visitors and serves beer, wine, non-alcoholic drinks , and food from Wolf in the Woods. Take a selfie with a megalodon shark, see scientists at work in our Paleo Center , admire glittering gems, get a close up look at spiders and snakes, and so much more. Best of all, get a look at our brand-new exhibition, Washed Ashore: Art to Save the Sea and grab a drink in the dive bar while chatting with a scientist. On select dates, channel your inner artist with Sketchparty , get competitive during trivia, or unwind while listening to the rooftop DJ. Hungry for more? The Craft Taco , located inside the Atrium, is a vibrant taco restaurant offering a delectable fusion of flavors and artisanal creations. They offer made-to-order tacos featuring signature blue corn tortillas, delectable burritos and bowls, and a variety of drinks and coffees. Admission is half-price after 5 PM, and parking is free after 6 PM. You can buy your tickets online in advance or buy them at the door the night of . As always, members of The Nat and Explorer pass holders enjoy free general admission.

title: Sacred Movement, Painted Prayers
address: 1439 El Prado, San Diego, CA, 92102
description: Experience the intersection of living craft, tradition, and movement. Begin the evening with a performance of Nihon Buyo —Japanese classical dance—by acclaimed dancer Ichinosuke Umekawa. Formally trained in ballet and Kabuki theater, Umekawa brings folk narratives to life through fluid grace and masterful expression. Following the performance, join Guest Curator Meher McArthur to enjoy an advance preview of Painted Prayers — The Japanese Folk Art Tradition of Ema before the exhibition opens to the public the next day. McArthur will share her research and insights into these hand-painted wooden prayer tablets, illuminating the rich connections between sacred visual art, human devotion, and performing craft.

description: Candlelight Concerts are a series of original music concerts created by Fever aimed at democratizing access to culture by allowing people all over the world to enjoy live music candlelit performances played by local musicians in various stunning locations illuminated by thousands of candles. Candlelight was initially conceived as a classical music series with concerts featuring works from the greatest composers, such as Vivaldi, Mozart, and Chopin. Now, the ever-growing list of programs includes a wide variety of themes and genres, including tributes to contemporary like Queen, ABBA, Coldplay, and Ed Sheeran, as well as shows dedicated to K-Pop, movie soundtracks and many more. This multi-sensory experience has also evolved to feature different elements, such as ballet dancers or aerial performers, as well as other genres, such as jazz, soul, opera, flamenco, and more. Candlelight Concerts are present in more than 100 cities worldwide, with over 3 Million guests in attendance to date

title: Ageless Artists Art Show and Fair 2026
venue: The San Diego LGBT Community Center
source: The San Diego LGBT Community Center
description: This intergenerational exhibition showcases original artwork by LGBTQ+ older adult and youth artists, celebrating creativity, storytelling, and meaningful connections across generations. Featuring Senior & youth artists Community art displays Intergenerational connection Creative expression for all ages We invite art lovers, friends, family, and the public to enjoy an afternoon filled with stunning artwork. Many artists will also have their pieces available for purchase—please note that most artists can only accept cash payments. Artists interested in exhibiting their work must RSVP. Space is limited, and tables will be assigned on a first-come, first-served basis. Don’t miss this wonderful celebration of art, community, and creativity! This activity is funded in part by City of San Diego Cultural Affairs and the Prebys Foundation. Place: The Center’s Auditorium Time: 1 pm to 4 pm Date: Saturday, October 17, 2026 Email For Information: seniors@thecentersd.org Art Submission Submit your artwork at: bit.ly/ageless-art-application Application Deadline: October 2, 2026 LGBTQ+ artists ages 50+ Submit photos of your artwork Space is limited Youth artists interested in participating: contact youthservices@thecentersd.org If selected, artists are responsible for setting up and displaying the work for the show. Tables provided upon request.

title: HIV & STI Screenings – Saturdays
venue: The San Diego LGBT Community Center
source: The San Diego LGBT Community Center
description: It's time for self-care with our free, confidential HIV/HCV testing and STI screenings in a compassionate and sex-positive environment with connections to health care and resources. Make your appointment today - call us at 619.487.9980 or email bethegeneration@thecentersd.org to make an appointment. We are open Monday-Friday 10am-7pm and Saturdays 10am-3pm by appointment. Walk-ins will be accepted based on availability. Please note that we do not offer MPOX testing as part of our testing services, please call 211 for testing assistance. Es hora de cuidarte con nuestras pruebas gratuitas y confidenciales de VIH/VHC y exámenes de detección de ITS en un entorno compasivo y sexualmente positivo con conexiones con recursos y atención médica. Haz tu cita hoy: llámanos al 619.487.9980 o envía un correo electrónico a bethegeneration@thecentersd.org para programar una cita. Abrimos de lunes a viernes de 10am a 7pm y sabados de 10am a 3pm con cita previa. Se aceptarán visitas sin cita previa según disponibilidad. Ten en cuenta que no ofrecemos pruebas MPOX como parte de nuestros servicios de pruebas; llame al 211 para obtener ayuda con las pruebas.

The Fleet Science Center strives to be an inclusive place where people of all needs and abilities are welcome and respectfully accommodated every day. Science is for everyone. Noise-canceling headsets are available for use during your visit to the Fleet Science Center. Please inquire at the ticket counter or at the Heikoff Giant Dome Theater. title: Hawktober at Lake Morena
venue: Lake Morena County Park,2550 Lake Morena Dr, Campo, CA 91906, USA
description: Hawktober is our annual celebration of local birds of prey, including hawks, owls, and falcons. This marks the event's eighth year offering FREE workshops at parks, campgrounds and wilderness preserves across San Diego County.  Events are free and open to all ages, starting October 3. Explore multiple workshops to meet different birds and rangers.  What to Expect:    * Live raptors: Meet ambassador birds like hawks, owls, and falcons up close and learn about their unique behaviors and adaptations.   * Fun facts: Discover how these birds live, what they eat, how they hunt, when they're active, and special traits like speed, camouflage, or night vision.   * Bird tales: Each event features different birds—each with a name and story—shared by passionate rangers.   * Special perk: Grab limited-edition Hawktober trading cards (while supplies last), complete with stats like wingspan, weight, and fun facts.  For more information, visit sdparks.org/hawktober https://www.sdparks.org/hawktober/ .

description: Sensory-Friendly Quiet Mornings at the Museum The Museum’s sensory-friendly quiet hours are held every Sunday from 10 a.m. to 11 a.m. This time is dedicated to creating a calmer, quieter museum experience. We remain open to the public during this time, and all are welcome to visit the Museum. During this time, specific exhibit features in the main Museum building will be turned off to minimize audio and visual stimulation. Noise-blocking headphones are free for check-out at the main Admissions desk and the entrance to the Cannibals: Myth & Reality exhibition, Exhibit features in the Cannibals: Myth & Reality exhibit will remain on, and all exhibits will be fully turned on at 11 a.m. Admission purchased during sensory-friendly quiet hours is the same as standard admission and applies to the entire day. Please contact publicprograms@museumofus.org with any questions.

title: Crisis Services Drop-In at SBYC
venue: The San Diego LGBT Community Center
source: The San Diego LGBT Community Center
description: A member of The Center's Crisis Services team will be available for drop-in times at South Bay Youth Center every Monday. Come talk to our Client Crisis Responder & Community Advocate about any crisis support services you may need. At our Crisis Services Drop-In at SBYC, you can receive a variety of services and support. See some examples below. Case management Domestic Violence and Abuse: Support for those experiencing intimate partner violence, domestic abuse, or other forms of violence within the LGBTQ+ community. Safe housing options and advocacy for survivors of domestic violence. Homelessness: Assistance for LGBTQ+ youth and adults who are homeless or at risk of homelessness, including emergency housing, shelter, and resources to help stabilize living conditions. Discrimination and Hate Crimes: Advocacy and legal support for individuals facing discrimination, harassment, or violence due to their sexual orientation or gender identity. Crisis services for those impacted by hate crimes or discrimination at work, in housing, or in other areas of life. Youth Support and Crisis Services: Specific programs for LGBTQ+ youth, including crisis intervention, safe spaces, peer support groups, and resources for those facing bullying or rejection due to their sexual orientation or gender identity. Family Supportive services: Some services provide educational materials and resources to families, helping them understand mental health conditions, warning signs, and effective ways to intervene & working with parents in navigating acceptance of their LGBTQ family member. Support groups allow family members of individuals experiencing a mental health crisis to connect with others going through similar situations. These groups provide emotional support, practical advice, and strategies for dealing with challenges. Referrals for Mental Health Crises: Counseling and therapy services for individuals experiencing anxiety, depression, or other mental health challenges, especially related to LGBTQ+ identity. Crisis intervention for individuals in immediate emotional distress or struggling with suicidal thoughts. Healthcare and Medical Needs: Crisis support related to health care access, including mental health care, HIV services, and assistance navigating medical challenges. Crisis intervention for those affected by HIV/AIDS, including support for individuals facing health emergencies. Transgender Services: Support for transgender individuals navigating identity-related crises, including gender dysphoria, coming out, or accessing gender-affirming care and services. SBYC is located at 1180 Third Ave. Suite C1, Chula Vista, CA, 91911

description: Pointeworks presents COMPOSITIONS: An Evening of Katie Jenkins, a celebration of Resident Composer Katie Jenkins featuring three original ballet commissions performed with live music. Curated by Artistic Director Sophie Williams, the evening brings together an international cast of world-class artists for a program dedicated entirely to female voices in both choreography and composition. The program features the return of Laine Habony's Chasing Shadows, a striking piano solo work, alongside Jacquelyn Long's Moving Forces for six dancers, piano, and violin. title: Hawktober at Waterfront Park
venue: Waterfront Park,1600 Pacific Hwy, San Diego, CA 92101, USA
description: Hawktober is our annual celebration of local birds of prey, including hawks, owls, and falcons. This marks the event's eighth year offering FREE workshops at parks, campgrounds and wilderness preserves across San Diego County.  Events are free and open to all ages, starting October 3. Explore multiple workshops to meet different birds and rangers.  What to Expect:    * Live raptors: Meet ambassador birds like hawks, owls, and falcons up close and learn about their unique behaviors and adaptations.   * Fun facts: Discover how these birds live, what they eat, how they hunt, when they're active, and special traits like speed, camouflage, or night vision.   * Bird tales: Each event features different birds—each with a name and story—shared by passionate rangers.   * Special perk: Grab limited-edition Hawktober trading cards (while supplies last), complete with stats like wingspan, weight, and fun facts.  For more information, visit sdparks.org/hawktober https://www.sdparks.org/hawktober/ .

description: <p>Join this free 10-week program on health education, physical activity, and healthy eating.</p> <p>During the 10 weeks you will:</p> <ul> <li>Receive education about caring for your health to prevent chronic illnesses such as diabetes, high blood pressure, being overweight, and high cholesterol. </li> <li>Learn the importance of portion sizes, nutritional content of foods, and the best ways to prepare them to obtain the greatest possible benefit for your health. </li> <li>Learn how incorporating physical activity supports your health through Bailoterapia (dance‑therapy) classes. </li> <li>Gain tools that support proper management of your emotions and your emotional well‑being. </li> </ul> <p>*This program is facilitated in Spanish.</p> <p>For more information, contact: Claudia: (619) 361-4819</p><p></p> <p>Únase a este programa gratuito de 10 semanas sobre educación en salud, actividad física y comida saludable.</p> <p>Durante las 10 semanas usted:</p> <ul><li>Obtendrá educación sobre el cuidado de su salud para prevenir el desarrollo de enfermedades crónicas como diabetes, presión arterial alta, sobre peso y colesterol.</li><li>Aprenderá la importancia del tamaño de las porciones, el contenido nutritivo de los alimentos y la mejor manera de prepararlos para obtener el mayor beneficio posible para su salud.</li><li>Aprenderá cómo la incorporación de actividad física apoya su salud por medio de clases de Bailoterapia.</li><li>Obtendrá herramientas que le apoyen al manejo adecuado de sus emociones y su bienestar emocional.</li></ul> <p>Este programa se imparte en español.</p> <p>Para obtener más informacíon, póngase en contacto con: Claudia: (619) 361-4819</p>

description: This is a support and discussion group for all people who identify on the aromantic spectrum, or asexual spectrum, or both. Those questioning are also welcome. Aromantic is a romantic orientation defined as having little to no romantic attraction or desire. Asexuality is a sexual orientation defined as having little to no sexual attraction or desire. Like all sexualities and romantic orientations, there is a spectrum of experiences, in which all are valid. This group is for ages 18 and up. description: It's time for self-care with our free, confidential HIV/HCV testing and STI screenings in a compassionate and sex-positive environment with connections to health care and resources. Es hora de cuidarte con nuestras pruebas gratuitas y confidenciales de VIH/VHC y exámenes de detección de ITS en un entorno compasivo y sexualmente positivo con conexiones con recursos y atención médica. title: Vienna Royal Orchestra: Viva Mozart 270
description: VIENNA ROYAL ORCHESTRA:VIVA MOZART 270 Matthew Busse, Conductor Tian Jiang,Piano Shay Mowbray, piano Anson Wong, piano From Carnegie Hall to Jacobs Music Center... Following its New York performance this summer at Carnegie Hall, the Vienna Royal Orchestra brings its VIVA MOZART 270 celebration to Jacobs Music Center in San Diego. This special concert honors the 270th anniversary of the birth of Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart, one of history's most beloved and influential musical geniuses. Audiences will enjoy an inspiring program of Mozart's timeless masterpieces, performed by distinguished musicians from Europe and the United States. Internationally celebrated pianist Tian Jiang appears as soloist in Mozart's Piano Concerto No. 23 in A Major, K. 488. Praised as "a thoughtful interpreter" by The New York Times and "a deeply persuasive Mozartean" by The Los Angeles Times, he is recognized for performances that combine poetic artistry, technical mastery, and expressive depth.

Email Tiffany.Nguyen@sdcounty.ca.gov</p><p><strong>What's in the Toolkit?</strong></p> <p>Kill-A-Watt Meter</p><p>Infrared Laser Thermometer</p><p>Refrigerator Thermometer</p><p>Water Thermometer</p><p>Water Pressure Gauge</p><p>Drip Gauge</p><p>Pliers</p><p>Step-by Step User Guide</p><p><br></p><p></p><p></p>

source: The San Diego LGBT Community Center
description: It's time for self-care with our free, confidential HIV/HCV testing and STI screenings in a compassionate and sex-positive environment with connections to health care and resources. Make your appointment today - call us at 619.487.9980 or email bethegeneration@thecentersd.org to make an appointment. We are open Monday-Friday 10am-7pm and Saturdays 10am-3pm by appointment. Walk-ins will be accepted based on availability. Please note that we do not offer MPOX testing as part of our testing services, please call 211 for testing assistance. Es hora de cuidarte con nuestras pruebas gratuitas y confidenciales de VIH/VHC y exámenes de detección de ITS en un entorno compasivo y sexualmente positivo con conexiones con recursos y atención médica. Haz tu cita hoy: llámanos al 619.487.9980 o envía un correo electrónico a bethegeneration@thecentersd.org para programar una cita. Abrimos de lunes a viernes de 10am a 7pm y sabados de 10am a 3pm con cita previa. Se aceptarán visitas sin cita previa según disponibilidad. Ten en cuenta que no ofrecemos pruebas MPOX como parte de nuestros servicios de pruebas; llame al 211 para obtener ayuda con las pruebas.

title: Book Talk- The Zoo Lady: How Belle Benchley Built the SD Zoo
description: <p>Listen to author Sandra E. Bonura discuss her book <em>The Zoo Lady: How Belle Benchley Built the San Diego Zoo</em>. <em></em></p><p>Belle Benchley was hired out of desperation, but she led with defiance. At just five feet tall, she navigated the San Diego Zoo through the brink of bankruptcy to become the world's first female zoo director. While novels like West with Giraffes capture the era's magic, the true drama lies in Benchley's own engineering. She didn't just manage animals. She orchestrated a cross-continental journey for the giraffes that redefined what was possible.</p> <p>Her legacy changed the world. An outsider to the scientific establishment, she rejected Victorian cages and pioneered the open-air, moated enclosures we see in modern zoos today. She spent her days in the trenches, developing an intuitive sense for animal care that often baffled trained veterinarians.</p> <p>Bonura is reclaiming the story of "The Zoo Lady." First, she saved the institution from collapse. Then, she built it into a global icon of conservation history.</p>

title: Painted Prayers: Japanese Ema Votive Plaques
address: 1439 El Prado, San Diego, CA, 92102
description: Ema (literally, “picture horse”) are wooden votive plaques on which visitors to Shinto shrines and Buddhist temples have for centuries written their prayers and wishes for the _kami _or Buddhist deities to read. Though these plaques originally featured horses, they evolved to feature many different images associated with various wishes, from good fortune to health to love and relationships. In conjunction with the exhibition Painted Prayers: The Japanese Folk Art Tradition of Ema , exhibition curator and Japanese art historian, Meher McArthur will explore the history of these votive plaques, the meanings behind some of the images, and their role in contemporary Japanese spiritual culture.

description: Join Latin@x Services at The San Diego LGBT Community Center for Festival Mictlan: Celebration of the Underworld—a family-centered gathering honoring Mictlan, the underworld in Mexica (Aztec) tradition, the sacred destination where souls journey and return on Día de los Muertos. We warmly invite you, your family, and community to come together in celebration, honoring our traditions while creating new memories through art, music, and collective joy. Where: Latine Pride - Liberty Station Central Promenade, 2641 Truxtun Rd. San Diego CA 92106 When: October 24, 2026 RSVP for the event and to participate in our contest at bit.ly/festival-mictlan Sing With Us: We Need Your Voice For Ecos del Mictlán, we’re forming a community choir to sing an original arrangement of “La Llorona y La Bruja,” alongside Tijuana Queer Coral, Coro Meraki, and singers from San Diego. You do NOT have to speak Spanish! Rehearsals are fully bilingual, and it’s just a few hours before the festival. Music is one of the most powerful ways to show we are united and will not be oppressed any longer. There is power when our voices rise together. If you are interested, please fill out our online form. Honor your loved ones at Festival Mictlan's Altar Contest. Altares will be displayed throughout the festival as offerings of memory and love, and top altars take home cash prizes. October 24, 2026 2–7 PM Latine Pride, Liberty Station Central Promenade 1st: $500 | 2nd: $300 | 3rd: $150 Registration closes October 9. Sign up at the link in our bio or bit.ly/festival-mictlan-2026.

description: It's time for self-care with our free, confidential HIV/HCV testing and STI screenings in a compassionate and sex-positive environment with connections to health care and resources. Walk-ins will be accepted based on availability. Please note that we do not offer MPOX testing as part of our testing services, please call 211 for testing assistance. Haz tu cita hoy: llámanos al 619.487.9980 o envía un correo electrónico a bethegeneration@thecentersd.org para programar una cita. Abrimos de lunes a viernes de 10am a 7pm y sabados de 10am a 3pm con cita previa. Se aceptarán visitas sin cita previa según disponibilidad. title: A Coven of Witches: Author Event & Craft with Alexis Powell
description: <p><strong><em>Double, double toil and trouble;<br>Fire burn and caldron bubble.</em></strong><strong></strong></p> <p><em>Hee-hee-hee!</em> Join us for a magical evening with author Alexis Powell and her brand new book, "A Coven of Witches: Spellbinding Tales of Magic and Myth." <br>Attendees with enjoy: </p> <ul><li>A live reading</li><li>Learn about the strange, whimsical, and unsettling lore on witches from all over the world</li><li>Q&A with the author</li><li>Book Signing</li><li>Craft your own witch hat and crescent moon wreath!<br><br></li></ul> <figure style="float: left; margin: 0px 10px 10px 0px;"><img src="https://sdcl.bibliocommons.com/events/uploads/images/full/a1eef5cf527048870482987119f36c16/a-coven-of-witches-9781423669784_hr.jpg" data-image="6a4ff92d4523092f002ed8f0" width="199.36986301369865" height="266" style="width: 199.37px; height: 266px;"></figure> <p><strong>About the Book</strong></p> <p><strong>A Coven of Witches</strong>: <br>Spellbinding Tales of Magic and Myth <br>(Frights to Tell at Night)<br>by <a href="https://www.alexiskpowell.com/home" target="_blank">Alexis Powell</a>, illustrated by Marina Vidal</p> <p>A spellbinding collection of 20 original spooky tales that reimagine witches from folklore, myth, and history. Read them before bedtime or share them to spook your friends—if you dare!<br><br>A girl receives a Christmas gift far worse than coal. A strange sideshow lures in new recruits. A birthday party turns into a grisly scavenger hunt. A werewolf stalks a ghostly graveyard. A train ride proves quite deadly. These stories are as enchanting as they are eerie, shining a light on the magical world of these legendary witches.<br><br>Features stories inspired by Baba Yaga, Marie Laveau, Circe, the Salem Witch Trials, La Lechuza, and more, all brought to life through gorgeous full-color illustrations.</p>

title: Hawktober at Lamar County Park
venue: Lamar County Park,3180 Bancroft Dr, Spring Valley, CA 91977, USA
description: Hawktober is our annual celebration of local birds of prey, including hawks, owls, and falcons. This marks the event's eighth year offering FREE workshops at parks, campgrounds and wilderness preserves across San Diego County.  Events are free and open to all ages, starting October 3. Explore multiple workshops to meet different birds and rangers.  What to Expect:    * Live raptors: Meet ambassador birds like hawks, owls, and falcons up close and learn about their unique behaviors and adaptations.   * Fun facts: Discover how these birds live, what they eat, how they hunt, when they're active, and special traits like speed, camouflage, or night vision.   * Bird tales: Each event features different birds—each with a name and story—shared by passionate rangers.   * Special perk: Grab limited-edition Hawktober trading cards (while supplies last), complete with stats like wingspan, weight, and fun facts.  For more information, visit sdparks.org/hawktober https://www.sdparks.org/hawktober/ .

description: Making jokes is what Rigoletto does for a living, serving as court jester to the predatory Duke of Mantua.
