title: Koto Lessons
address: 2215 Pan American Road East, San Diego, CA, 92101
description: Koto, also called kin, long Japanese board zither having 13 silk strings and movable bridges. The body of the instrument is made of paulownia wood and is about 190 cm (74 inches) long. When the performer is kneeling or seated on the floor, the koto is held off the floor by two legs or a bridge-storage box; in most modern concerts, the instrument is placed on a stand so the performer can sit on a chair. The koto is played by plucking the strings with the thumb and first two fingers of the right hand, which are fitted with ivory plectrums called tsume. The left hand, in traditions after the 16th century, may alter the pitch or sound of each string by pressing or manipulating the strings to the left of the bridges. Various pentatonic tunings are used, depending on the type of music being played. The koto appeared in the Japanese court during the 8th century and was called the gakusō. Schools for the bourgeois were established in the 16th century. Two of these—Ikuta (started in the 17th century) and Yamada (opened in the 18th century)—continue to the present day. Solo (danmono) and chamber (sankyoku) music dominate the repertory, and in the latter form the koto player often sings as well. title: Art in the Evening: The Moods of Early Russian Art
description: Join us for a special Art in the Evening program featuring Justin Willson, Curator at The Icon Museum and Study Center in Clinton, Massachusetts, as he illuminates one of the most transformative periods in Russian icon painting. Drawing upon exceptional works in the Timken collection, Willson will trace developments in style and patronage across fifteenth- and sixteenth-century Muscovy, beginning with painters in the circle of Dionisiy and revealing how a sweeping religious revival reshaped the artistic and spiritual character of early Russian art. Set against the intimate backdrop of the Museum’s galleries, the evening offers a rare opportunity to experience the Timken’s distinguished collection of Russian icons through the perspective of a leading scholar in the field. Guests are invited to enjoy wine and curated nibbles before the lecture, followed by an engaging conversation that brings new insight to works whose beauty and spiritual resonance have endured for centuries. The lecture coincides with the release of Wilson’s book, The Moods of Early Russian Art (University of Chicago Press, 2026). Copies of the book will be available for purchase at the event.

description: Join award-winning Chef Spencer Hunter of Lia’s Lumpia on October 25, 2026, from 6:00–8:00 PM at the San Diego History Center for a Kamayan feast celebrating Filipino American History Month. A San Diego native and finalist on Food Network’s Great Food Truck Race, Chef Spencer honors his Filipino grandmother’s culinary legacy while blending it with his African American roots. He has taken first place for his Sisig Lumpia, cheffed for distinguished clientele ranging from corporate leaders to members of the British Royal Family, and continues to redefine what modern fusion cuisine can be. Kamayan is a traditional Filipino style of communal dining where food is spread across a table lined with fresh banana leaves and shared by everyone. title: Crisis Services Drop-In at SBYC
venue: The San Diego LGBT Community Center
source: The San Diego LGBT Community Center
description: A member of The Center's Crisis Services team will be available for drop-in times at South Bay Youth Center every Monday. Come talk to our Client Crisis Responder & Community Advocate about any crisis support services you may need. At our Crisis Services Drop-In at SBYC, you can receive a variety of services and support. See some examples below. Case management Domestic Violence and Abuse: Support for those experiencing intimate partner violence, domestic abuse, or other forms of violence within the LGBTQ+ community. Safe housing options and advocacy for survivors of domestic violence. Homelessness: Assistance for LGBTQ+ youth and adults who are homeless or at risk of homelessness, including emergency housing, shelter, and resources to help stabilize living conditions. Discrimination and Hate Crimes: Advocacy and legal support for individuals facing discrimination, harassment, or violence due to their sexual orientation or gender identity. Crisis services for those impacted by hate crimes or discrimination at work, in housing, or in other areas of life. Youth Support and Crisis Services: Specific programs for LGBTQ+ youth, including crisis intervention, safe spaces, peer support groups, and resources for those facing bullying or rejection due to their sexual orientation or gender identity. Family Supportive services: Some services provide educational materials and resources to families, helping them understand mental health conditions, warning signs, and effective ways to intervene & working with parents in navigating acceptance of their LGBTQ family member. Support groups allow family members of individuals experiencing a mental health crisis to connect with others going through similar situations. These groups provide emotional support, practical advice, and strategies for dealing with challenges. Referrals for Mental Health Crises: Counseling and therapy services for individuals experiencing anxiety, depression, or other mental health challenges, especially related to LGBTQ+ identity. Crisis intervention for individuals in immediate emotional distress or struggling with suicidal thoughts. Healthcare and Medical Needs: Crisis support related to health care access, including mental health care, HIV services, and assistance navigating medical challenges. Crisis intervention for those affected by HIV/AIDS, including support for individuals facing health emergencies. Transgender Services: Support for transgender individuals navigating identity-related crises, including gender dysphoria, coming out, or accessing gender-affirming care and services. SBYC is located at 1180 Third Ave. Suite C1, Chula Vista, CA, 91911

title: Art + Design Workshop: Floral Arranging
description: Celebrate the beauty and abundance of the season with a morning of floral design at the Timken. Inspired by the rich colors, textures, and graceful compositions found in the Museum’s collection, this hands-on workshop invites participants to create an elegant autumn arrangement using a thoughtfully selected palette of seasonal flowers and foliage. Under the guidance of a professional floral designer, participants will explore the principles of balance, color, form, and movement that unite the traditions of painting and floral design. Each guest will create a distinctive arrangement to take home. No prior floral design experience is necessary. Workshop fee includes all materials, tools, and light refreshments. About the Artist: Anne Latham is a floral designer, photographer, ceramicist, garden designer, and artist. As the principal designer of Three Swords Floral Co., she leads an exceptional team of designers, traveling around California and Hawai’i to craft floral experiences for private estates, destination weddings, and discreet brand activations. Anne has been flowering since 2015, following her formal training as a bookbinder and lithographer at the School of the Art Institute of Chicago. Her Midwestern roots and background as an artist, studio assistant, and time spent in the hospitality industry continue to inform her refined, grounded, and deeply personal approach to floral design.

source: The San Diego LGBT Community Center
description: It's time for self-care with our free, confidential HIV/HCV testing and STI screenings in a compassionate and sex-positive environment with connections to health care and resources. Walk-ins will be accepted based on availability. Please note that we do not offer MPOX testing as part of our testing services, please call 211 for testing assistance. Es hora de cuidarte con nuestras pruebas gratuitas y confidenciales de VIH/VHC y exámenes de detección de ITS en un entorno compasivo y sexualmente positivo con conexiones con recursos y atención médica. Haz tu cita hoy: llámanos al 619.487.9980 o envía un correo electrónico a bethegeneration@thecentersd.org para programar una cita. Abrimos de lunes a viernes de 10am a 7pm y sabados de 10am a 3pm con cita previa. Se aceptarán visitas sin cita previa según disponibilidad. Ten en cuenta que no ofrecemos pruebas MPOX como parte de nuestros servicios de pruebas; llame al 211 para obtener ayuda con las pruebas.

title: Dr. Jekyll & Mr. Hyde (1920) Played by David Marsh
description: Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde (1920) Witness one of silent cinema's most chilling performances in Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde! John Barrymore delivers a mesmerizing transformation in this dark tale of science gone horribly wrong, as a brilliant doctor unleashes his sinister alter ego with shocking consequences that spiral beyond his control. Join us for this gripping and gothic masterpiece featuring live organ accompaniment tailored to the film by David Marsh. Arrive early and stay late for fun and informative activities! This screening is part of our Silent Movie Mondays series at the Balboa Theatre. Join us at this historic venue and step back a century, when audiences cheered, the organ came alive, and silent films glowed on the big screen. Learn more at sandiegotheatres.org.

description: <p>On alternating Tuesdays, we'll have Project NexTech teaching basic engineering and natural science in a fun way!  This week, the maker space workshop will cover engineering concepts through fun and simple challenges like popsicle stick bridges, spaghetti and marshmallow towers, wooden cars, and more!  No sign-up required; for ages 6-13.  </p>

title: Homework & Hangout | Asistencia de tareas
description: <p>High school students offer homework help, reading practice, and craft activities for grades K-8. Drop in on Tuesdays between 5:00-6:30. This program runs from October through November and February through April.</p> <p>This program will take a break on the following days:</p> <ul><li>November 24, 2026</li><li>March 23, 2027</li><li>March 30, 2027</li></ul> <p>Estudiantes de secundaria ofrecen ayuda gratuita con tareas y lectura, además de manualidades. Para niños del kínder hasta el grado 8. Tutores bilingües en español están disponibles. Venga sin registrarse los martes de las 5:00 hasta las 6:30. Desde el octubre hasta el noviembre y desde febrero hasta el abril.</p> <p>Este programa tomará un descanso estos días festivos:</p> <ul><li><strong></strong>24 de noviembre de 2026</li><li>23 de marzo de 2027</li><li>30 de marzo de 2027</li></ul>

title: Writing Workshop: Generative Memoir
description: <p>When you talk about your life, do people say you should write a book? Now’s the time to start. No matter where you are in your memoir-writing journey, this creative writing workshop will help you start, develop, or revise a memoir-in-process. We’ll work through a series of writing prompts, exploring ways to get unstuck, using specifics and sensory imagery, and scene building. Bring paper and a pencil.</p><p>Suzanne Roberts is the author of <em>Animal Bodies: On Death, Desire, and Other Difficulties</em> (Longlisted for the PEN/Diamonstein-Spielvogel Award for the Art of the Essay);​<em> Bad Tourist: Misadventures in Love and Travel</em> (North American Travel Journalists Association Bronze Award for a Travel Book); <em>Almost Somewhere: Twenty-Eight Days on the John Muir Trail </em>(Winner of the National Outdoor Book Award); four collections of poems; and a craft book: <em>52 Writing Prompts: Inspiration for the Creative Writer</em>. Named “The Next Great Travel Writer” by National Geographic’s <em>Traveler</em>, Suzanne's work has been listed as notable in <em>Best American Essays</em>, included in <em>The Best Women's Travel Writing</em>, and has recently appeared in <em>The New York Times, Ploughshares, National Geographic, CNN, The Fourth Genre, </em><em>and </em><em>Brevity, </em>among others. She holds a doctorate in literature and the environment from the University of Nevada-Reno and teaches in the low residency MFA in creative writing at UNR-Tahoe. <br></p>

title: HIV & STI Screenings
venue: The San Diego LGBT Community Center
source: The San Diego LGBT Community Center
description: It's time for self-care with our free, confidential HIV/HCV testing and STI screenings in a compassionate and sex-positive environment with connections to health care and resources. Make your appointment today - call us at 619.487.9980 or email bethegeneration@thecentersd.org to make an appointment. We are open Monday-Friday 10am-7pm and Saturdays 10am-3pm by appointment. Walk-ins will be accepted based on availability. Please note that we do not offer MPOX testing as part of our testing services, please call 211 for testing assistance. Haz tu cita hoy: llámanos al 619.487.9980 o envía un correo electrónico a bethegeneration@thecentersd.org para programar una cita. Abrimos de lunes a viernes de 10am a 7pm y sabados de 10am a 3pm con cita previa. Se aceptarán visitas sin cita previa según disponibilidad. Ten en cuenta que no ofrecemos pruebas MPOX como parte de nuestros servicios de pruebas; llame al 211 para obtener ayuda con las pruebas.

source: The San Diego LGBT Community Center
description: This group serves as a social gathering space for Trans Masc individuals to discuss and receive support and/or guidance on transitioning and life events. Transmasculine is an umbrella term used to describe someone who was assigned female at birth and who identifies either their gender identity or gender expression as masculine in any way. Transmasculine community members include but are not limited to: transgender men, demiboys, nonbinary, two-spirit, and gender-fluid people. Es hora de cuidarte con nuestras pruebas gratuitas y confidenciales de VIH/VHC y exámenes de detección de ITS en un entorno compasivo y sexualmente positivo con conexiones con recursos y atención médica. Just curiosity, support, and community. Your goals. Your pace. Your journey. When: Thursdays, 5:00 – 6:00 PM Where: The Center, 3909 Centre St, San Diego Contact: counseling@thecentersd.org

description: Join our VIRTUAL Wellness Wednesday Yoga Class! Each session features a mindful and rejuvenating yoga practice designed specifically for teens to build strength, flexibility, balance, and focus. SD Nights - short for San Diego/Safe Destination Nights - is a FREE program developed by the County of San Diego Department of Parks and Recreation designed to provide teens, ages 10 to 18, with safe places to recreate after school and during critical hours. title: Volcanoes: The Fires of Creation
address: 1875 El Prado, San Diego, CA, 92101
description: Volcanoes have helped create our world. The continents, the air we breathe and even life itself have their origins in fire. These processes have created extraordinary ecosystems and wildlife habitats. The story of volcanoes is the story of the planet’s creation and the story of us. Volcanoes: The Fires of Creation , lets you witness the 2018 Kilauea eruption in Hawaii; see the archaeological remains of Pompeii, devastated almost 2,000 years ago by Mount Vesuvius; visit Mount Fuji in Japan, made up of three volcanoes—Fuji on top and two others hidden beneath; and marvel at the black molten lava of Ol Doinyo Lengai in Tanzania.

title: HIV & STI Screenings
venue: The San Diego LGBT Community Center
source: The San Diego LGBT Community Center
description: It's time for self-care with our free, confidential HIV/HCV testing and STI screenings in a compassionate and sex-positive environment with connections to health care and resources. Make your appointment today - call us at 619.487.9980 or email bethegeneration@thecentersd.org to make an appointment. We are open Monday-Friday 10am-7pm and Saturdays 10am-3pm by appointment. Walk-ins will be accepted based on availability. Please note that we do not offer MPOX testing as part of our testing services, please call 211 for testing assistance. Es hora de cuidarte con nuestras pruebas gratuitas y confidenciales de VIH/VHC y exámenes de detección de ITS en un entorno compasivo y sexualmente positivo con conexiones con recursos y atención médica. Haz tu cita hoy: llámanos al 619.487.9980 o envía un correo electrónico a bethegeneration@thecentersd.org para programar una cita. Abrimos de lunes a viernes de 10am a 7pm y sabados de 10am a 3pm con cita previa. Se aceptarán visitas sin cita previa según disponibilidad. Ten en cuenta que no ofrecemos pruebas MPOX como parte de nuestros servicios de pruebas; llame al 211 para obtener ayuda con las pruebas.

source: The San Diego LGBT Community Center
description: Join us for Social Meetups at Hillcrest Youth Center - come check out what we have to offer! These meetups are for ages 18-24. When: Fridays, 3-7pm Where: 514 Pennsylvania Ave., San Diego, CA 92103 Contact: Email HYC@thecentersd.org or call (619) 692-2077 x626 Hillcrest Youth Center services include: Safe & Affirming LGBTQI+ space, support groups, mental health resources Computer lab, community closet, snacks, video games, arts & crafts Gender affirming supplies, hormone replacement therapy referrals Name and gender marker change, sharp disposal, sexual health supplies Basic needs resources, school supplies, hygiene products & more! Please note that we provide hormone replacement therapy referrals and name and gender marker change referrals to people 18 and over. If you're interested and under 18, we can also talk to your parent(s)/guardian(s) to get them informed. In the state of California, anyone under the age of 18 must obtain parental consent to receive medical care.

title: HIV & STI Screenings – Saturdays
venue: The San Diego LGBT Community Center
source: The San Diego LGBT Community Center
description: It's time for self-care with our free, confidential HIV/HCV testing and STI screenings in a compassionate and sex-positive environment with connections to health care and resources. Make your appointment today - call us at 619.487.9980 or email bethegeneration@thecentersd.org to make an appointment. We are open Monday-Friday 10am-7pm and Saturdays 10am-3pm by appointment. Walk-ins will be accepted based on availability. Please note that we do not offer MPOX testing as part of our testing services, please call 211 for testing assistance. Es hora de cuidarte con nuestras pruebas gratuitas y confidenciales de VIH/VHC y exámenes de detección de ITS en un entorno compasivo y sexualmente positivo con conexiones con recursos y atención médica. Haz tu cita hoy: llámanos al 619.487.9980 o envía un correo electrónico a bethegeneration@thecentersd.org para programar una cita. Abrimos de lunes a viernes de 10am a 7pm y sabados de 10am a 3pm con cita previa. Se aceptarán visitas sin cita previa según disponibilidad. Ten en cuenta que no ofrecemos pruebas MPOX como parte de nuestros servicios de pruebas; llame al 211 para obtener ayuda con las pruebas.

title: Hawktober at El Monte County Park
venue: El Monte County Park,15805 El Monte Rd, Lakeside, CA 92040, USA
description: Hawktober is our annual celebration of local birds of prey, including hawks, owls, and falcons. This marks the event's eighth year offering FREE workshops at parks, campgrounds and wilderness preserves across San Diego County.  Events are free and open to all ages, starting October 3. Explore multiple workshops to meet different birds and rangers.  What to Expect:    * Live raptors: Meet ambassador birds like hawks, owls, and falcons up close and learn about their unique behaviors and adaptations.   * Fun facts: Discover how these birds live, what they eat, how they hunt, when they're active, and special traits like speed, camouflage, or night vision.   * Bird tales: Each event features different birds—each with a name and story—shared by passionate rangers.   * Special perk: Grab limited-edition Hawktober trading cards (while supplies last), complete with stats like wingspan, weight, and fun facts.  For more information, visit sdparks.org/hawktober https://www.sdparks.org/hawktober/ .

title: More Than Pink Walk
address: San Diego, CA
description: The MORE THAN PINK Walk, Susan G. Komen’s largest fundraising event series, evolved from the Race for the Cure in 2018. Each year, we host over 100,000 participants at our 40+ in-person (and one virtual) walks across the U.S. Since the first Walk in 2018, our participants have raised more than $60 million dollars and continue to be a part of a community committed to our vision of a world without breast cancer. With inclusive and accessible options for people of all ages and abilities – including breast cancer survivors, those currently in treatment for breast cancer and people living with metastatic breast cancer – the Walk provides participants the opportunity to come together and connect in meaningful ways. It allows us to focus on sharing our passion, sharing our stories and connecting with others, all while fundraising to support life-saving programs and research. Our finish line is a world without breast cancer, and we know the only way we can get there is together.

description: Sensory-Friendly Quiet Mornings at the Museum The Museum’s sensory-friendly quiet hours are held every Sunday from 10 a.m. to 11 a.m. This time is dedicated to creating a calmer, quieter museum experience. We remain open to the public during this time, and all are welcome to visit the Museum. During this time, specific exhibit features in the main Museum building will be turned off to minimize audio and visual stimulation. Noise-blocking headphones are free for check-out at the main Admissions desk and the entrance to the Cannibals: Myth & Reality exhibition, Exhibit features in the Cannibals: Myth & Reality exhibit will remain on, and all exhibits will be fully turned on at 11 a.m. Admission purchased during sensory-friendly quiet hours is the same as standard admission and applies to the entire day. Please contact publicprograms@museumofus.org with any questions.

title: Día de los Muertos at SDMA
address: 1450 El Prado, San Diego, CA, 92101
description: Come together with family, friends, and the community at large at a special, free community event celebrating and honoring Día de los Muertos. Enjoy live performances, family-friendly art-making activities, and a special Día de los Muertos ofrenda created by visiting artist Betsabeé Romero in collaboration with local San Diego students, all in the Balboa Park Plaza de Panama in front of The San Diego Museum of Art and free to the community. Through artist-designed artmaking activities, community members will be invited to honor loved ones, share memories, and contribute meaningful objects and creative responses to the ofrenda on view in the plaza. Romero will join the Museum community for the inauguration of the SDMA ofrenda on Sunday, November 1 at 11:00 a.m. on the Museum’s front steps. The Taco Party , a gathering featuring unlimited street-style tacos, refreshing beverages, music, and a festive atmosphere, is a ticketed event complementing Día de los Muertos at SDMA. Free admission to The San Diego Museum of Art (SDMA) and the Museum of Photographic Arts at The San Diego Museum of Art (MOPA@SDMA) on Sunday, November 1 at noon–5:00 p.m. further complements the Día de los Muertos celebration.

title: Tusk: The Classic Fleetwood Mac Tribute

TUSK features note-perfect renditions of both the solo and full band songs, with each member specializing in one of the core lineup of Fleetwood Mac (Lindsey Buckingham, Stevie Nicks, Christine McVie, John McVie, and Mick Fleetwood). Truly the best at what they do, TUSK is unmatched in their tribute to one of the greatest bands of all time.

description: Join Ranger Craig for a hike through the sage brush and chapparal of San Dieguito County Park. Starting at the butterfly garden in the lower park, this will be an approximately hour long and 2-3 mile hike discussing the native plants and animals that make San Diego County the most biodiverse in the country. Meets monthly on every first Sunday.  Parking: $5  For more information, call (858) 755-2386

title: The Outsiders (Touring)
description: Adapted from S.E. HINTON's seminal novel and FRANCIS FORD COPPOLA's iconic film, this thrilling new musical features a book by ADAM RAPP with JUSTIN LEVINE, music and lyrics by JAMESTOWN REVIVAL (Jonathan Clay & Zach Chance) & Tony Award® winner JUSTIN LEVINE, music supervision, orchestration, & arrangements by JUSTIN LEVINE, choreography by RICK KUPERMAN & JEFF KUPERMAN, & direction by Tony Award® winner DANYA TAYMOR. Entertainment Weekly says, "THE OUTSIDERS has the power to inspire an entire generation." In Tulsa, Oklahoma, 1967, Ponyboy Curtis, his best friend Johnny Cade and their Greaser family of 'outsiders' battle with their affluent rivals, the Socs. THE OUTSIDERS navigates the complexities of self-discovery as the Greasers dream about who they want to become in a world that may never accept them. With a dynamic original score, THE OUTSIDERS is a story of friendship, family, belonging..and the realization that there is still "lots of good in the world."

description: Tour the solar system with the Fleet’s resident astronomer and connect with other skywatchers. Journey through the cosmos with us as we explore a new topic each month. The Sky Tonight: Virtual Edition at 7 p.m. on the third Wednesday of each month, via Zoom NEW! The Sky Tonight: Family Edition at 11 a.m. on the second Sunday of each month Presentations begin with a look at the sky followed by a special topic presentation. Before or after Wednesday shows at the Fleet, join members of the San Diego Astronomy Association on the Prado by the Bea Evenson Fountain and be inspired by the stars in the actual night sky (weather permitting) through different telescopes.

title: Spinning Resistance: Women, Cloth, and the Long Memory of 1776
address: 1649 El Prado, Suite #3, San Diego, CA, 92101
description: The spinning wheel keeps showing up at moments of political crisis — and it’s never just about spinning. In the 1760s, American women turned spinning bees into public acts of resistance against British taxation. Arts and Crafts reformers claimed it as a rebuke to industrial capitalism. In the 1920s, Gandhi made the charkha the emblem of Indian independence from the British Empire. Twentieth-century American women, meanwhile, rediscovered it as a symbol of a revolutionary female tradition the original 1776 had denied them — decorating their homes with it, wearing the loose clothing it evoked, claiming the Daughters of Liberty as their own foremothers. But the spinning wheel casts a longer shadow: enslaved women spun and wove too, and the cotton that fed industrial production had been harvested by coerced labor for generations. Join the San Diego History Center for another program in our America at 250 series as historian Molly McClain explores the history of the spinning wheel across three continents and 150 years to ask what commemorative culture commemorates — and who gets to decide. Molly McClain (PhD, Yale) is a professor of history at the University of San Diego. Her research focuses on women’s history, philanthropy, and cultural history more broadly. A ninth-generation San Diegan, she is the author of four books and numerous articles, including Ellen Browning Scripps: New Money and American Philanthropy (2017). McClain’s public history work includes over a decade as editor of The Journal of San Diego History and the successful designation of the La Jolla Park Coastal Historic District to the National Register of Historic Places in 2024. General tickets: $20 Museum Members: $10

description: Adapted from S.E. HINTON's seminal novel and FRANCIS FORD COPPOLA's iconic film, this thrilling new musical features a book by ADAM RAPP with JUSTIN LEVINE, music and lyrics by JAMESTOWN REVIVAL (Jonathan Clay & Zach Chance) & Tony Award® winner JUSTIN LEVINE, music supervision, orchestration, & arrangements by JUSTIN LEVINE, choreography by RICK KUPERMAN & JEFF KUPERMAN, & direction by Tony Award® winner DANYA TAYMOR. Entertainment Weekly says, "THE OUTSIDERS has the power to inspire an entire generation." In Tulsa, Oklahoma, 1967, Ponyboy Curtis, his best friend Johnny Cade and their Greaser family of 'outsiders' battle with their affluent rivals, the Socs. THE OUTSIDERS navigates the complexities of self-discovery as the Greasers dream about who they want to become in a world that may never accept them. With a dynamic original score, THE OUTSIDERS is a story of friendship, family, belonging..and the realization that there is still "lots of good in the world."

title: Felt Together
address: 1439 El Prado, San Diego, CA, 92102
description: Inspired by the intricate bas-relief needlework and cozy scenes featured in My Bed: Enchanting Ways to Fall Asleep Around the World , our newest Together workshop series, Felt Together , explores the art of needle felting. The series is led by Sophie Ancel, a fiber artist who blends rich textures and thoughtful layering to bring imaginative landscapes to life. Through her process-driven approach to wool and textile art, she brings a warm, accessible perspective to the world of living craft. Friday, November 6, 2026 | 5-7pm In November, create a night sky scene out of wool. Sophie will teach you how to layer and mix colorful fibers to build a cozy scene with glowing windows, trees, and stars. The Together series at Mingei invites makers of all skill levels to come together and create in a supportive, low-pressure environment. Past iterations— Sew Together, Weave Together , Dye Together , Stitch Together , Clay Together, and Knot Together —explore a variety of craft techniques while emphasizing collaboration, experimentation, and hands-on learning. Each workshop encourages participants to connect with materials, try new skills, and enjoy the process of making together.

title: The Outsiders (Touring)
description: Adapted from S.E. HINTON's seminal novel and FRANCIS FORD COPPOLA's iconic film, this thrilling new musical features a book by ADAM RAPP with JUSTIN LEVINE, music and lyrics by JAMESTOWN REVIVAL (Jonathan Clay & Zach Chance) & Tony Award® winner JUSTIN LEVINE, music supervision, orchestration, & arrangements by JUSTIN LEVINE, choreography by RICK KUPERMAN & JEFF KUPERMAN, & direction by Tony Award® winner DANYA TAYMOR. Entertainment Weekly says, "THE OUTSIDERS has the power to inspire an entire generation." In Tulsa, Oklahoma, 1967, Ponyboy Curtis, his best friend Johnny Cade and their Greaser family of 'outsiders' battle with their affluent rivals, the Socs. THE OUTSIDERS navigates the complexities of self-discovery as the Greasers dream about who they want to become in a world that may never accept them. With a dynamic original score, THE OUTSIDERS is a story of friendship, family, belonging..and the realization that there is still "lots of good in the world."

title: The Surge: An Ode to Sinead O'Connor
description: Tony Award-winning choreographer Sonya Tayeh brings her singular vision to The Surge: An Ode to Sinéad O?Connor, a world-premiere dance-theater work inspired by her uncompromising spirit. Set to O?Connor?s iconic music and featuring narration from her memoir Rememberings, the performance explores protest, faith, vulnerability, and the courage to defy expectation. Performed by a company of ten women with more than five hundred years of collective experience, The Surge challenges fear around aging and honors the beauty, strength, and perspective that come with time. Fierce and tender, this evening of dance honors O?Connor?s legacy through artists whose lives bring depth, wisdom, and lived experience to the stage.

title: The Outsiders (Touring)
description: Adapted from S.E. HINTON's seminal novel and FRANCIS FORD COPPOLA's iconic film, this thrilling new musical features a book by ADAM RAPP with JUSTIN LEVINE, music and lyrics by JAMESTOWN REVIVAL (Jonathan Clay & Zach Chance) & Tony Award® winner JUSTIN LEVINE, music supervision, orchestration, & arrangements by JUSTIN LEVINE, choreography by RICK KUPERMAN & JEFF KUPERMAN, & direction by Tony Award® winner DANYA TAYMOR. Entertainment Weekly says, "THE OUTSIDERS has the power to inspire an entire generation." In Tulsa, Oklahoma, 1967, Ponyboy Curtis, his best friend Johnny Cade and their Greaser family of 'outsiders' battle with their affluent rivals, the Socs. THE OUTSIDERS navigates the complexities of self-discovery as the Greasers dream about who they want to become in a world that may never accept them. With a dynamic original score, THE OUTSIDERS is a story of friendship, family, belonging..and the realization that there is still "lots of good in the world."

description: Sensory-Friendly Quiet Mornings at the Museum The Museum’s sensory-friendly quiet hours are held every Sunday from 10 a.m. to 11 a.m. This time is dedicated to creating a calmer, quieter museum experience. We remain open to the public during this time, and all are welcome to visit the Museum. During this time, specific exhibit features in the main Museum building will be turned off to minimize audio and visual stimulation. Noise-blocking headphones are free for check-out at the main Admissions desk and the entrance to the Cannibals: Myth & Reality exhibition, Exhibit features in the Cannibals: Myth & Reality exhibit will remain on, and all exhibits will be fully turned on at 11 a.m. Admission purchased during sensory-friendly quiet hours is the same as standard admission and applies to the entire day. Please contact publicprograms@museumofus.org with any questions.

title: The Outsiders (Touring)
description: Adapted from S.E. HINTON's seminal novel and FRANCIS FORD COPPOLA's iconic film, this thrilling new musical features a book by ADAM RAPP with JUSTIN LEVINE, music and lyrics by JAMESTOWN REVIVAL (Jonathan Clay & Zach Chance) & Tony Award® winner JUSTIN LEVINE, music supervision, orchestration, & arrangements by JUSTIN LEVINE, choreography by RICK KUPERMAN & JEFF KUPERMAN, & direction by Tony Award® winner DANYA TAYMOR. Entertainment Weekly says, "THE OUTSIDERS has the power to inspire an entire generation." In Tulsa, Oklahoma, 1967, Ponyboy Curtis, his best friend Johnny Cade and their Greaser family of 'outsiders' battle with their affluent rivals, the Socs. THE OUTSIDERS navigates the complexities of self-discovery as the Greasers dream about who they want to become in a world that may never accept them. With a dynamic original score, THE OUTSIDERS is a story of friendship, family, belonging..and the realization that there is still "lots of good in the world."

House in the Gaslamp Quarter delivers one of the most interactive live music experiences in downtown San Diego. PARKING $12 Flat-Rate Parking for 3 hours at Horton Plaza Parking Garage w/ validation. Regular rates apply after 3 hours. Ask your server for validation sticker. The Best Dueling Piano Show in San Diego When it comes to live music and nightlife in San Diego, The Shout! House is one of the Gaslamp Quarter’s most exciting destinations. Expect sing-alongs, comedy, audience participation, staff dancing on stage, and music ranging from classic rock anthems to today’s biggest hits. No two shows are ever the same — the audience helps create the experience. Private Events & Group Parties Planning a birthday party, corporate event, bachelor or bachelorette celebration, or group night out in San Diego? The Shout! House is one of the most unique private event venues in the Gaslamp Quarter. Enjoy live entertainment, great food, craft cocktails, and a high-energy atmosphere your guests will never forget. Reserve your table today and Laugh, Sing & Shout the night away.

title: Susan G Komen 3 Day Walk
address: San Diego, CA
description: Your Susan G. Komen 3-Day ® starts the moment you make the commitment. Your 3-Day coaches will support you as you train and fundraise. Our amazing community of walkers, crew, and volunteers will welcome you into our Pink Bubble as you get ready to take an incredible journey to end breast cancer forever. You can customize your journey with a 1-Day, 2-Day or full 3-Day experience. Choose whichever commitment, distance and fundraising minimum is right for you. Every step matters. Every dollar raised helps us fulfill our mission. 1 DAY, 20 MILES Raise $750. A great way to sample the 3-Day experience, Sunday, November 15. 2 DAYS, 40 MILES Raise $1,800. Step it up for an extra challenge, Saturday and Sunday, November 14-15. 3 DAYS, 60 MILES Raise $2,300. Join us for the full 3-Day experience, Friday, Saturday and Sunday, November 13-15. When you choose the 3-Day Route , your first day begins with an inspirational Opening Ceremony where the adrenaline and anticipation of taking on 60 miles is like nothing you’ve ever experienced before. The feelings of pride and strength you’ll realize while walking 60 miles through San Diego’s cool surfside neighborhoods are only matched by the spirit and gratitude of the communities you encounter and those you are helping along the way. You’ll walk along the Pacific Coast Highway and will be wowed by the beauty of Del Mar, Torrey Pines and Mission Bay! You’ll spend Friday and Saturday night with your fellow participants in our outdoor camp at Sunset Point Park. Hotel options are available at your own expense . When you choose the 2-Day Route , your first day begins on Saturday, November 14 with an energetic welcome and walk out. You’ll walk approximately 40 miles over the course of two days, with breaks and lunch along the route. You’ll join us at the end of your first day for a moving Honor Ceremony where we honor and share stories of those we’ve lost, those still fighting and our survivors and thrivers living with metastatic breast cancer. You’ll spend Saturday night with your fellow participants in our outdoor camp at Sunset Point Park, with an option to camp on Friday night as well, if you wish. When you choose the 1-Day Route , your journey begins Sunday, November 15 where you join in with our 2-Day and 3-Day walkers for a welcome and walk out on the final day of the 3-Day journey. Or you can choose to arrive on Saturday and spend the night with us in camp. For all participants, your adventure culminates in a Finish Line Festival and Closing Ceremony celebrating all you’ve accomplished, remembering those we have lost, and honoring those who are in the fight of their lives. Whether you walk 20, 40 or 60 miles, you’ll do so in the embrace of the dedicated 3-Day community, sharing stories, eating meals together and making new friends. There’s no question that the 3-Day is a hard journey, but we all know, it’s not as hard as breast cancer. It’s not as hard as getting bad news at your latest scan. It’s not as hard as saying goodbye. We walk because we must. We walk for ourselves, our sisters, mothers, fathers, daughters, sons and friends. We walk because we can’t sit idly by watching while breast cancer still exists in the world. Since 2003, we’ve raised more than $927 million to save lives, support community programs, and make huge strides in breast cancer research and access to care. The Susan G. Komen 3-Day is an experience you’ll never forget. It’s why our walkers come back year after year to recommit their time and energy to put an end to breast cancer once and for all. Register and join us.

Go behind the scenes of Mavor’s creative process and learn where it began, how it’s evolved, and what continues to inspire her work. title: Star Party at Oakoasis
venue: Oakoasis County Preserve,12620 Wildcat Canyon Rd, Lakeside, CA 92040, USA
description: Come see real Astronomers from the San Diego Astronomy Association and look through their big, beautiful telescopes at Mother Nature's night light display. The evening starts off with a short, ranger-led, twilight hike in the preserve.  It may be too cold to see bats and scorpions, but it should be a great night for stargazing! The evening continues with stars and refreshments.  Come early to get a good parking spot and face your lights away from the telescopes so when you leave you won't blind them. Dress warmly and bring a flashlight.  Cloud cover or inclement weather may cancel. Call Ranger Kyle ahead for status or if you're lost: 858-699-8668.  For general park information: 619-561-0580

description: Sensory-Friendly Quiet Mornings at the Museum The Museum’s sensory-friendly quiet hours are held every Sunday from 10 a.m. to 11 a.m. This time is dedicated to creating a calmer, quieter museum experience. We remain open to the public during this time, and all are welcome to visit the Museum. During this time, specific exhibit features in the main Museum building will be turned off to minimize audio and visual stimulation. Noise-blocking headphones are free for check-out at the main Admissions desk and the entrance to the Cannibals: Myth & Reality exhibition, Exhibit features in the Cannibals: Myth & Reality exhibit will remain on, and all exhibits will be fully turned on at 11 a.m. Admission purchased during sensory-friendly quiet hours is the same as standard admission and applies to the entire day. Please contact publicprograms@museumofus.org with any questions.

description: Koto, also called kin, long Japanese board zither having 13 silk strings and movable bridges. The body of the instrument is made of paulownia wood and is about 190 cm (74 inches) long. When the performer is kneeling or seated on the floor, the koto is held off the floor by two legs or a bridge-storage box; in most modern concerts, the instrument is placed on a stand so the performer can sit on a chair. The koto is played by plucking the strings with the thumb and first two fingers of the right hand, which are fitted with ivory plectrums called tsume. The left hand, in traditions after the 16th century, may alter the pitch or sound of each string by pressing or manipulating the strings to the left of the bridges. Various pentatonic tunings are used, depending on the type of music being played. The koto appeared in the Japanese court during the 8th century and was called the gakusō. Schools for the bourgeois were established in the 16th century. Two of these—Ikuta (started in the 17th century) and Yamada (opened in the 18th century)—continue to the present day. Solo (danmono) and chamber (sankyoku) music dominate the repertory, and in the latter form the koto player often sings as well. One on One Lessons JFGM Member $55 | Non-Member $75 Upper Garden | Education Center 1 Hour Length Koto and materials included Registration Required, Admission included

title: Fiesta Island Time Trials Fiesta Island Time Trials is
venue: 1258 E Mission Bay Dr. San Diego , CA United States
description: Fiesta Island Time Trials Fiesta Island Time Trials is San Diego's original time trial series since 1968, sponsored by San Diego Bicycle Club. Time trials are known as the race of truth, it is the cyclist against the clock. Athletes select category and distance, 3 laps (20km) or 6 laps (40km) around Fiesta Island, juniors will ride one or two laps. Single riders, tandems, and teams all compete for top honors and island records or come out and test their fitness. An awards ceremony will be held after the last athlete finishes. Top six finishers in each category will be eligible to earn points towards series competition. Awards will be given to series winners at the last race of the series.

title: Wine & Masters: Beyond Champagne
description: From the storied vineyards of Champagne to the hills of northern Italy, Catalonia, England, and California, sparkling wine takes on a distinctive character shaped by place, tradition, and technique. This lively exploration travels beyond Champagne to reveal how celebrated sparkling wines—including Prosecco, Cava, Franciacorta, Sekt, and emerging New World expressions—reflect the grapes, landscapes, and cultures from which they come. Along the way, discover what distinguishes each style and why the world’s fascination with bubbles extends far beyond France. About the Speaker: Dane Kuta is a Level 2 Certified Sommelier, Champagne Master, Bordeaux Master, Champagne MOOC, Italian Wine Professional, and Napa Valley Wine Expert. He has taught wine appreciation at San Diego State University; California State University, San Marcos; and MiraCosta College and is a member of the Guild of Sommeliers. PROGRAM 4:00 – 4:30 Wine & Hors d’Oeuvres Reception 4:30 – 5:15 Part One: Lecture with Dane Kuta 5:15 – 5:30 Dessert Intermission 5:30 – 6:30 Part Two: Sparkling Wine Tasting ‍

title: Jo Koy: Koy Meets World Tour
description: Jo Koy is one of today?s premier stand-up comedians, rising from performing in a Vegas coffee house to selling out arenas worldwide. His relatable comedy, drawn from his colorful family and Filipino heritage, has connected with audiences across cultures, making him one of the top 10 grossing stand-up comedians each year according to Pollstar and Billboard. In 2023, Koy inked a two-special deal with Netflix, with the first special released in 2024. Jo Koy: Live From Brooklyn, filmed at the historic King?s Theatre, premiered globally on June 4 and was the #6 most viewed special that year, with over 240 million minutes watched. He recently filmed his upcoming Netflix special in Stockton, CA, set to release later this year. Koy starred in the 2022 Universal Pictures comedy Easter Sunday, inspired by his life and Filipino roots. He has also appeared in Disney?s Haunted Mansion, voiced characters in Netflix?s Monkey King and Leo, and most recently in Paramount+?s The Tiger?s Apprentice.
